author: redhuang-0622
body:
## Summary by Sourcery

为 AI 面试官添加流式 TTS 播放功能，并提升音频录制、ASR 以及线程生命周期管理的健壮性。

New Features:
- 引入流式音频播放器和 token-to-TTS 流水线，将面试官的 token 流转换为实时语音输出。
- 添加音频压缩辅助工具，将录制的 WAV 文件转换为压缩格式（默认 MP3），在压缩失败时可优雅地回退到原始 WAV。
- 在提问和追问阶段启用可选的面试官语音播放，由现有的面试流式流程驱动。

Bug Fixes:
- 通过安全关闭语音和 ASR 线程，并在窗口关闭时进行清理，避免 QThread 生命周期问题和潜在崩溃。
- 更稳健地处理录音和 ASR 失败情况，即使发生异常也能安全关闭音频流并终止 PyAudio 实例。
- 通过在面试官 TTS 流水线中对 token 和近期播放的句子去重，减少重复或多次播放的 TTS 语音。

Enhancements:
- 使用归一化峰值/均方根（peak/RMS）指标细化静音和音量检测，以提升 VAD 和输入校验的准确性。
- 为音频流处理和句子分割添加类型注解和工具辅助方法，以提升语音 SDK 的可维护性和清晰度。
- 改进面试官流式体验，根据面试阶段自动开始和停止 TTS，并保持报告阶段静音。

Build:
- 添加 dashscope 依赖，以支持基于 DashScope 的流式 TTS 集成。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Add streaming TTS playback for the AI interviewer and improve robustness of audio recording, ASR, and thread lifecycle management.

New Features:
- Introduce a streaming audio player and token-to-TTS pipeline to convert interviewer token streams into real-time spoken audio.
- Add an audio compression helper to convert recorded WAV files to compressed formats (default MP3) with graceful fallback to raw WAV when compression fails.
- Enable optional interviewer voice playback during question and follow-up phases, driven by the existing interview streaming flow.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent QThread lifecycle issues and potential crashes by safely shutting down voice and ASR threads, and cleaning up on window close.
- Handle recorder and ASR failures more robustly by safely closing audio streams and terminating PyAudio instances even on exceptions.
- Reduce duplicated or repeated TTS playback by de-duplicating tokens and recently played sentences in the interviewer TTS pipeline.

Enhancements:
- Refine audio recording silence and volume detection using normalized peak/RMS metrics for more accurate VAD and input validation.
- Add type hints and utility helpers for audio stream handling and sentence segmentation to improve maintainability and clarity of the voice SDK.
- Improve interviewer streaming UX by automatically starting and stopping TTS according to interview phases and keeping report phase silent.

Build:
- Add dashscope as a dependency to support DashScope-based streaming TTS integration.

</details>

author: kaitranntt
body:
## Problem

Clicking a conversation from the Chat page's initial state (no session selected) does not load messages. The URL updates, sidebar highlights the conversation, but the main area shows "Start a conversation" placeholder. Only after clicking a different conversation do messages load.

Closes #729

## Visual Review

[Full comparison report](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/kaitranntt/goclaw/blob/d0344adacb266acdafe77e4ee027744500e7bfeb/.github/pr-assets/730/index.html)

### Chat — First Click from Clean State

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaitranntt/goclaw/d0344adacb266acdafe77e4ee027744500e7bfeb/.github/pr-assets/730/before-chat-first-click.png) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaitranntt/goclaw/d0344adacb266acdafe77e4ee027744500e7bfeb/.github/pr-assets/730/after-chat-first-click.png) |

Before: Clicking "Chat a95c8ffa" from initial state — conversation highlighted but main area shows empty "Start a conversation" placeholder.
After: Same click — conversation messages load immediately on first click.

All captures: same instance (claw backend), same user (kai/Master), same agent (glm thục bô), same conversation. Callout borders mark the review area.

## Root Cause

`skipNextHistoryRef` was unconditionally set to `true` whenever `sessionKey` transitioned from empty to non-empty (line 61 in `use-chat-messages.ts`). This skip was intended **only** for the new-chat send flow, where an optimistic user message is already displayed and `loadHistory()` would race with `chat.send`. However, it also fired when clicking an existing conversation from the sidebar — preventing `loadHistory()` from running.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `ui/web/src/pages/chat/hooks/use-chat-messages.ts` | Guard `skipNextHistoryRef` with `expectingRunRef.current` check |

## Validation

- [x] `pnpm run build` passes
- [x] Bug reproduced via Playwright against live GoClaw instance
- [x] RPC log confirmed `chat.history` was never called on first click
- [x] Fix verified via local dev server — messages load on first click
- [x] New-chat send flow preserved (expectingRunRef is set by useChatSend before ws.call)
- [x] Before/after UI evidence captured with matching state

author: shellicar
body:
Two small UX bugs.

## Startup banner pushed off screen

`showStartupBanner` was called before `addHistoryBlocks`, making the banner the first block in the conversation. On sessions with enough history to fill the viewport it scrolled off the top and was never visible.

Moved the call to after history replay so the banner always sits immediately above the first prompt.

## Left/right cycling collapses expanded tool input

`selectPrev` and `selectNext` both set `#toolExpanded = false`, so pressing an arrow key while a tool's input was expanded would immediately collapse it. `resetExpanded` (called on return to editor mode) already handles the right teardown point.

Removed the collapse from `selectPrev` and `selectNext` so expanded state is preserved while navigating between tools.

| Fix `initDmart` return type | `dmart_base.dart:100` | Changed `void` to `Future<void>` so callers can properly `await` it |

| Fix `late final` crash | `action_response.dart:57` | Changed `late final` to a regular `final` field with constructor param, preventing `LateInitializationError` |
| Fix `Bearer null` on public endpoints | `dmart_base.dart` (multiple) | `getManifest`, `getSettings`, `getPayload`, `retrieveEntry`, `query` now only send auth header when token is non-null |

| Fix | File(s) | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|

| Rename `SortyType` → `SortType` | `sort_type.dart`, `query_request.dart`, `dmart_base.dart` | Fixed typo in enum name |

body:
## Summary                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                        
  - Add `metadata_into_note_type` procedure in `crates/miden-protocol/asm/protocol/note.masm` that extracts the note    
  type (public/private) from the metadata header
  - Add unit tests for both public and private note types, similar to `test_active_note_get_sender`                     
                                                                                                                        
  Closes https://github.com/0xMiden/protocol/issues/2737                                                                
                                                                                                                        
  ## Context      

  As suggested by @PhilippGackstatter in [#2636                                                                         
  (comment)](https://github.com/0xMiden/protocol/pull/2636/files#r3036541747), the note type extraction logic should
  live in `note.masm` as a reusable procedure rather than being inlined in individual note scripts.                     
                  
  The first felt of the metadata header has the following layout:                                                       
  [sender_id_suffix (56 bits) | reserved (3 bits) | note_type (1 bit) | version (4 bits)]
                                                                                                                        
  The procedure extracts the single bit at position 4, where `0 = Private` and `1 = Public`.

  ## Test plan                                                                                                          
  
  - [x] `test_active_note_get_note_type_public` — verifies extraction returns `1` for public notes                      
  - [x] `test_active_note_get_note_type_private` — verifies extraction returns `0` for private notes

### Motivation
- Ensure the in-chat profile/name/status header is always visible and never scrolls out of view, including during message scrolling and mobile keyboard open/close events.

### Motivation
- The card flip was showing mirrored/front text at the end of the rotation instead of the real back face on some browsers (notably iPhone/Safari). 
- The intent is to keep the current visual layout and click behavior while fixing 3D rendering/backface bleed-through on Safari/iOS. 
- The fix must preserve `click` logic and the `entrar` button behavior while avoiding visual mirroring.

### Description
- Tighten 3D stacking by keeping `transform-style: preserve-3d` on the rotating container and adding explicit `-webkit-` prefixed transforms on the container and faces. 
- Make `.guest-card__inner` use `overflow: visible` and explicit base `transform: rotateY(0deg) translateZ(0)` and flipped `transform: rotateY(180deg) translateZ(0)` (with `-webkit-transform`) to avoid flattening on iOS. 
- Ensure each face has `backface-visibility: hidden` and small `translateZ(1px)` separation via `transform` (and `-webkit-transform`) to prevent z-fighting and mirrored bleed-through. 
- Add `.guest-card__face--front` with `rotateY(0deg) translateZ(1px)` and ensure `.guest-card__face--back` uses `rotateY(180deg) translateZ(1px)`; no JS changes were required to `renderGuestCards()` or click logic.

author: sirbrenton
body:
## Summary

Updates `capability.json` to reflect a new class of execution failure:

> **taxonomy present, enforcement missing**

Adds pattern:
- `taxonomy-present-but-not-enforced`

Based on:
- OMP issue #3126 (quota STOP misclassification collapsing retry path)
- Canonical receipt: `PT-2026-04-05-github-oh-my-openagent-3126-stop-name-known-retry-collapsed`

Also updates:
- corpus size: 25 → 26 receipts
- repos analyzed: + `code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent`
- date range latest: 2026-04-05
- version: 0.1.9 → 0.1.10
- last_updated: 2026-04-05

---

## Why this matters

This introduces a more mature failure mode than previously captured.

Earlier patterns covered:
- missing Retry-After
- missing classification
- incorrect classification

This pattern captures:

> **Correct classification exists — but is not enforced at the decision layer.**

In OMP #3126:
- `quotaexceedederror` was already distinguished from `ratelimiterror`
- but `isRetryableModelError` still returned `true` for both
- resulting in:
  - fallback retry loops
  - retry budget waste
  - failure to surface terminal conditions

The system *knew* the difference — but behaved as if it didn’t.

---

## New pattern

### taxonomy-present-but-not-enforced

- **Hazard:** rate_limit_429
- **Failure shape:**
  - STOP cases identified lexically
  - collapsed into retryable path at decision boundary
- **Classification:**
  - STOP known by name → treated as WAIT/retryable
- **Fix:**
  - STOP must short-circuit retry/fallback
  - classifier precedence: STOP before RETRYABLE
  - message-level quota signals must override generic retry logic

---

## Why this belongs in the corpus

Meets receipt criteria:

- **Real failure**: production retry collapse on quota exhaustion
- **Reusable pattern**: taxonomy ≠ enforcement is common across systems
- **Leverage**: small fix (precedence + STOP handling) eliminates entire class of retry waste

---

## Implication for Pitstop

This sharpens the thesis:

> Systems don’t just fail because they lack retry logic.  
> They fail because they collapse distinct failure modes into the same decision.

And further:

> Even when systems *have* the right taxonomy, they still fail if it isn’t enforced.

This is exactly the layer Pitstop targets.

---

## No breaking changes

- Manifest-only update
- No schema changes
- No receipt changes

---

## Next

- Continue tracking higher-order failure modes (classification vs enforcement vs routing)
- Look for additional instances of “taxonomy present but not enforced” across other repos

author: jaclark5
body:
# PostgreSQL Snowflake Startup Changes

- **Functional Improvement**: Prefer `pg_ctl` found directly on `PATH` before falling back to `pg_config`-based discovery in `PostgresHarness`.
  - **Why necessary**: Prevents mixed PostgreSQL toolchains (for example, `pg_config` from one installation and `pg_ctl`/`postgres` from another), which can cause fragile startup behavior after package manager upgrades.
  - **Platforms that benefit**: macOS (especially Homebrew users), Linux systems with multiple PostgreSQL installs, and CI environments with layered tool paths.

- **Debugging Enhancement**: Include PostgreSQL logfile path and log tail in startup failures raised by `PostgresHarness.start()`.
  - **Why necessary**: `pg_ctl` often returns generic errors like "could not start server"; surfacing log tail makes root-cause diagnosis immediate without manual file hunting.
  - **Platforms that benefit**: All platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows-like POSIX layers) where PostgreSQL logs are available.

- **Functional Improvement**: Add targeted detection of locale-related PostgreSQL startup failure and retry `pg_ctl start` once with `LC_ALL=C` and `LANG=C`.
  - **Why necessary**: Some environments export invalid locale state (for example empty `LC_ALL`), which can trigger PostgreSQL startup aborts; retrying only on known failure signatures avoids broad environment changes.
  - **Platforms that benefit**: Primarily macOS (where this failure was observed), and any Unix-like environment where locale configuration can be invalid in shell/notebook sessions.

- **Functional Improvement**: Add a PostgreSQL minimum version check in `qcfractal/db_socket/socket.py` before creating tables and running Alembic upgrades.
  - **Why necessary**: QCFractal schema features require PostgreSQL 15+ (for example `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` behavior in unique constraints); failing early with a clear message avoids hard-to-diagnose migration/runtime failures later.
  - **Platforms that benefit**: All platforms, especially environments with older default PostgreSQL versions (common on Linux distributions and long-lived workstation installs).

- **Debugging Enhancement**: Add explicit retry note text to the raised startup error when locale-safe retry was attempted.
  - **Why necessary**: Makes it clear in a single traceback whether fallback logic was used, reducing ambiguity during triage and PR review.
  - **Platforms that benefit**: All platforms.

Close #1000

author: shengyfu
body:
Replace the full mmap of `index.bin` (posting lists) with on-demand file reads via `seek+read`. Only `lookup.bin` (the sorted trigram lookup table) stays memory-mapped.

## Problem

tgrep mmaps both `lookup.bin` and `index.bin` entirely. For large repos (440k+ files), `index.bin` can be hundreds of MB, all of which becomes resident memory even though only a small fraction of posting lists are accessed per query.

## Solution

- `IndexReader.postings: Option<Mmap>` → `postings_file: Option<Mutex<File>>`
- `read_posting_entries()` now seeks to the exact offset and reads only the requested posting list bytes
- The lookup table (small, frequently binary-searched) remains mmap'd for fast access
- The `Mutex<File>` ensures thread-safe access since multiple query threads may read postings concurrently

## Tradeoffs

- **Pro**: Dramatically lower resident memory for large repos (only lookup table + file paths in memory)
- **Con**: Each posting list read is a syscall (seek + read) instead of a memory access. The OS page cache still helps for hot posting lists.

body:
Summary:

made TableStore::ingest_batch async so the new Rust-facing ingestion path no longer inherits the internal block_in_place bridge from DatabaseScanner.

the underlying table mutation is already async via LiveTableData::push. keeping TableStore::ingest_batch synchronous meant async Rust callers were forced through a hidden runtime constraint and needed a multi-thread tokio runtime. this change keeps the existing sync telemetry path intact and only makes the TableStore seam honest for downstream Rust callers.

updated the TableStore tests to await ingestion directly. downstream snapshot ingestion can now await ingest_batch normally instead of relying on the blocking bridge.

### Motivation
- Replace hardcoded `/confirm` parsing with a configurable confirmation prefix so confirmation parsing and guidance reflect runtime `commandPrefixMap.confirm`.
- Ensure structured confirmations like `archive|overwrite <target>` are validated against the active prefix and that plain `confirm` is only accepted when policy allows it.

### Description
- Updated `parseConfirmCommand` signature to `parseConfirmCommand(inputText, confirmPrefix)` and added `escapeRegexLiteral` to safely build a prefix regex; parsing now prefers the configured prefix and falls back to plain `confirm` only when the configured prefix is not literally `confirm`.
- Plumbed `commandPrefixMap.confirm` through call sites in `handleLocalApiRoute` and updated uses of `coercePendingConfirmRequirement`, `validatePendingConfirmation`, and `buildToolFollowupText` to accept the active prefix.
- Adjusted `coercePendingConfirmRequirement` to populate example strings using the provided confirm prefix, and tightened Tier B/C validation so plain confirmations are allowed only per `plain_confirm_allowed` policy and Tier C requires prefix + target form.
- Replaced hardcoded guidance strings (e.g. "Reply with /confirm" / "Reply with confirmation") with messages that reference the active `commandPrefixMap.confirm` and reflect whether plain `confirm` is permitted.
- All changes are contained in `server/localApi.ts` (parsing, coercion, validation, and tool follow-up message updates).

author: herauralite
body:
### Motivation
- Create a deterministic, backend-owned intervention-certifiability posture derived from existing assurability/dependability/predictability and upstream review states to avoid overclaiming certifiability. 
- Make the distinction between “certifiable” and “assurable-for-now” explicit so operator artifacts can surface whether a review supports certification-ready claims. 
- Provide clear blocking signals when reopenable pressure, novelty, split/conflict, sparse support, provisional verdicts, or assurability fragility make certifiability unstable. 
- Ensure new certifiability fields survive backfill/load/legacy world shapes and appear in canonical reporting artifacts.

### Description
- Added a certifiability pipeline producing `review_intervention_certifiability_state`, `operator_review_intervention_certifiability_evidence`, and `compact_historical_intervention_certifiability_lines` with deterministic logic that inspects assurability, dependability, predictability, reliability, repeatability and many upstream review states. 
- Introduced bounded certifiability signals (`intervention_certifiable_review`, `assurable_for_now_review`, `not_yet_intervention_certifiable_review`, `unresolved_review`) plus blocking flags (`blocked_by_reopenable_pressure`, `blocked_by_novelty`, `blocked_by_split_or_conflict`, `blocked_by_sparse_support`, `blocked_by_provisional_or_unstable_verdict`, `blocked_by_assurability_fragility`, and `weakly_intervention_certifiable_review`) and distinction metadata (`certification_stability_ready`, `assurable_but_certification_unstable_review`). 
- Propagated certifiability outputs into canonical artifacts and operator snapshots (scenario digest, operator brief, scenario handoff, scenario insight report) and added compact operator-facing lines and historical compact lines for quick evidence readout. 
- Hardened persistence/backfill and defaults so legacy saves infer reasonable `assurable_for_now` signals from existing assurability state and added backfill functions and scenario/world defaulting to avoid missing-field drift.

### Testing
- Compiled modified modules with `python -m compileall backend/app/services/auralite_reporting_service.py backend/app/services/auralite_world_service.py` which completed successfully. 
- Ran the backend test suite with `cd backend && pytest -q` which returned `1 passed` indicating existing tests still pass after the changes.

author: asheshgoplani
body:
## Summary

Fixes #387. The notify-daemon now checks whether the target (parent/conductor) session is currently `running` before delivering transition notifications via `tmux send-keys`.

- When the target is `running` (busy generating a response), delivery is **deferred** with result `deferred_target_busy`
- Deferred events are **not marked as notified**, so the next daemon poll cycle will retry delivery
- Once the target transitions to `waiting`/`idle`, the notification is delivered normally

## Changes

- **`transition_notifier.go`**: Added `transitionDeliveryDeferred` constant. In `dispatch()`, added status check (`parent.UpdateStatus()` + `GetStatusThreadSafe()`) before sending. In `NotifyTransition()`, deferred events skip `markNotified()` to allow retry.
- **`transition_notifier_test.go`**: Added `TestDeferredEventNotMarkedAsNotified` (verifies deferred events bypass dedup) and `TestResolveParentNotificationTargetSelfLoop` (edge case coverage).

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` passes
- [x] `go test -race ./internal/session/...` passes (all existing + 2 new tests)
- [ ] Manual: set up conductor + child, verify notification deferred while conductor is running, delivered when waiting

body:
### Motivation
- The preview card had inconsistent temporal direction and ambiguous labels that made it hard to understand the timeline and the 3-month seal window quickly.  
- The goal was to unify time direction (older → newer/current), make the seal window explicit as an ordered 3-slot sequence, and strengthen row titles and small explanatory copy without changing backend payload or business logic.  

### Description
- Sorted recent months chronologically before rendering so time flows left → right and the newest/current month is always on the right by using `orderedRecentMonths = [...recentMonths].sort(...).slice(-4)` in `PreviewAchievementCard.tsx`.  
- Replaced weak headings and labels with semantic titles: the seal row now shows `Seal window / Ventana al sello` and `3 consecutive months / 3 meses consecutivos`, and the history row now shows `Recent history / Historial reciente`.  
- Converted the 3-month window into explicit ordered slots with position labels (`Mes 1 / Mes 2 / Actual` or `Month 1 / Month 2 / Current`) and rendered slots as compact state chips (`rounded-md` chips with `data-slot-symbol`) rather than decorative circles so each slot reads as a checkpoint.  
- Made recent month items show visible month labels (via `monthLabel(...)`) and preserved current/projection marking; kept the donut score and added the small explanatory microcopy `current habit strength / fuerza actual del hábito`.  
- Added a concise bridge sentence clarifying the relationship between the two rows: `The window uses 3 consecutive months to determine if the seal is close.` / `La ventana usa 3 meses seguidos para indicar si el sello está cerca.`  
- Files changed: `apps/web/src/components/dashboard-v3/PreviewAchievementCard.tsx` and `apps/web/src/components/dashboard-v3/__tests__/PreviewAchievementCard.test.tsx` (updated tests to reflect labels, slot labeling, and chronological ordering).

author: liad242
body:
## Problem

When `enableRtl` is set to `true`, horizontal scrolling can cause the header and body viewports to desynchronize — the header scrolls but the body cells don't follow (or vice versa).

This happens because two places in the scroll sync chain read/write `scrollLeft` directly without using the RTL-aware helpers (`getScrollLeft` / `setScrollLeft`), which handle cross-browser differences in how `scrollLeft` behaves under RTL:
- Chrome/Safari use negative `scrollLeft` values in RTL
- Firefox uses positive (inverted) values
- The helpers normalize these to a consistent positive value

## Root Cause

**1. `RowContainerCtrl.getHScrollPosition()`** reads raw `this.eViewport.scrollLeft` instead of `_getScrollLeft(this.eViewport, this.enableRtl)`.

This returns browser-specific values to callers (e.g. `getHorizontalPixelRange()` API, drag-and-drop positioning) that expect normalized values.

**2. `HeaderRowContainerComp.setViewportScrollLeft()`** writes directly to `this.getGui().scrollLeft = left` instead of using `_setScrollLeft(this.getGui(), left, enableRtl)`.

The header receives a normalized scroll offset from the body's scroll handler, but writes it as a raw `scrollLeft` value. In Chrome RTL, the browser expects a negative value, but receives a positive one — causing the header to scroll to the wrong position.

## Fix

- `rowContainerCtrl.ts`: `getHScrollPosition()` now uses `_getScrollLeft(this.eViewport, this.enableRtl)`, consistent with `getCenterViewportScrollLeft()` and `getViewportScrollLeft()` in the same class.
- `headerRowContainerComp.ts`: `setViewportScrollLeft` now uses `_setScrollLeft(this.getGui(), left, enableRtl)`, consistent with `setCenterViewportScrollLeft()` in `RowContainerCtrl`.

Both fixes use the same RTL-aware helpers that are already correctly used everywhere else in the scroll sync chain.

## How to reproduce

1. Set `enableRtl: true` on the grid
2. Add enough columns so horizontal scrolling is required
3. Scroll horizontally — observe header and body cells become misaligned

Particularly reproducible in Chrome, where `scrollLeft` is negative in RTL mode.

body:
Nasamotor's sales processes (AML/ASAE compliance, B2B deals, bespoke financing) are tracked manually in Excel/SharePoint outside Autoline DMS. This document centralizes the analysis needed to select a digitalization approach.

## What's included

- **Side-by-side comparison table** across all three options (Standard Dev, Low-code, AI Agentic) covering: pros/cons, financials, maintenance, scalability, and decision criteria
- **Detailed breakdowns** per scenario with POC deliverables, cost ranges, and technology stack
  - Option 1: Custom app (.NET/Java/Node.js + React/Vue) — €120K–250K build, 6–9 month MVP
  - Option 2: Low-code (Power Apps/Mendix/OutSystems) — €25–75K/yr, <2 month POC
  - Option 3: AI Agentic (Copilot Studio + Azure OpenAI) — €30–120K initial, 6–10 week setup
- **Phased hybrid recommendation** tailored to Nasamotor's current state (disconnected DMS, manual AML flows, Power BI investment):
  ```
  Phase 1 (0–3mo):   Low-code POC → digitize AML/ASAE, immediate audit trail
  Phase 2 (3–9mo):   Custom dev → Autoline DMS integration, CRM, financing workflows
  Phase 3 (9–18mo):  AI Agentic overlay → NLQ, WhatsApp agent, predictive compliance
  ```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Sales Process Digitalization — POC Scenarios for Nasamotor

## Context
Nasamotor manages several sales/support processes (e.g., special deals, B2B bulk deals, bespoke financing, external approvals, specific compliance flows) that are not natively supported in their existing Autoline DMS. Current tracking is handled in Excel, SharePoint, or manually — leading to inefficiency, risk, and lack of auditability. Nasamotor aims to build a digital solution to centralize and streamline these workflows.

## Goal
Design a robust, scalable platform/application to support the missing sales processes and ensure smooth handoff, compliance, reporting, and scale-out across the organization.

## Scenarios
### Option 1: Standard Application Development
- Custom app (web/mobile) using .NET, Java, or Node.js plus modern frontend (React/Vue).
- Full integration with Autoline (API, CSV, batch), DMS, and Power BI.
- Supports complex logic, approval trees, notifications, document mgmt, audit trails.

#### POC Required:
- Wireframes + architecture plan
- Estimated dev time (6-9 months for MVP)
- Budget/ROI outline (dev, infra, 3y TCO)

**Pros:**
- Highest flexibility — can fit all edge processes
- Direct integration potential across systems
- Full control over security/compliance
**Cons:**
- Highest upfront/dev cost, slow changes
- Needs skilled team, ongoing maintainers
- Upgrades/refactors are slow
**Financial Impact:**
- €120K-250K build, €20-50K/yr ops
**Maintenance:**
- IT team needed for bugfix, patches, upgrades
**Scalability:**
- Scales by design if architected well; horizontal scaling possible
**Criteria:**
- Use when: process is core, company has IT maturity, ROI on custom fit is clear

---

### Option 2: Vibe Coding Approach (Low-code/No-code)
- Build with Power Apps, Mendix, OutSystems, ServiceNow.
- Drag-and-drop forms, workflow builder, out-of-box connectors (DMS, Power BI, mail).
- IT rapid prototyping; business can build/iterate with minimal code.

#### POC Required:
- App wireframes in platform of choice
- Timeline (<2 months for MVP, iteration fast)
- Budget/ROI (platform license, dev)

**Pros:**
- Rapid POC → production, iterate fast
- Lower dev cost/less IT dependency
- Built-in compliance/logging/user mgmt
- Scales well across departments
**Cons:**
- Vendor lock-in/platform constraints (feature gaps)
- Custom/complex logic can be hard to implement
- Integration sometimes limited w/ legacy DMS
**Financial Impact:**
- €25K-75K/yr license + build; low infra
**Maintenance:**
- Maintained by citizen devs + IT admin
**Scalability:**
- Good for workflow/process scale, hard for deep custom
**Criteria:**
- Use when: process is not strategic IP, needs fast change, low IT headcount

---

### Option 3: AI Agentic Approach
- Deploy an agentic AI orchestrator (e.g., Microsoft Copilot Studio + Azure OpenAI, agentic orchestration frameworks).
- Agents monitor triggers, converse with staff, automate most steps: data extraction (OCR), prefill, compliance, suggest next actions, escalate to human only if needed.
- Plugs into DMS, Power BI, email, WhatsApp, even voice.

#### POC Required:
- Demo prompt flows, workflow diagrams, pilot integration
- Estimate: 6-10 weeks setup, retraining as needed
**Pros:**
- Handles ambiguity/exception, adapts as processes change
- Automates not just workflow but data, docs, routine compliance
- Can scale up (volume) AND out (add new processes easily)
- Next-gen user experience: NLQ, actions via chat/voice
**Cons:**
- Cutting-edge — needs strong data foundations
- Human-AI interaction standards required; staff training
- Error handling, monitoring, and "explainability" are harder
**Financial Impact:**
- €30K-120K initial (varies), €20-40K/yr for AI services/ops
**Maintenance:**

body:
## Summary

- 新增 `model-catalog.ts`：从 openclaw CLI (`models list --all --json`) 加载 801 个模型的 input 能力目录，支持 awaitable loading、gateway ready 后自动重试、跨 provider fallback
- 新增 `resolveModelInput()` 统一入口：所有 input 写入路径（8 处）统一通过此函数，优先查 catalog，未命中时保守 fallback 到 `["text"]`
- `verifyProvider()` 返回 `supportsImage` 字段，前端保存配置时使用后端探测结果
- 移除 Setup/Settings 中的手动"图像支持"checkbox

## Motivation

用户选择纯文本模型（如 deepseek-chat）后，UI 仍允许图片输入，导致请求失败。之前用手动 checkbox 让用户自行标记，体验差且容易出错。现在从 openclaw 的权威模型目录自动检测。

## Key Design Decisions

- **保守 fallback**：catalog 未命中时默认 `["text"]`（宁可漏标图片能力，也不错标文本模型）
- **竞态解决**：`ensureCatalogLoaded()` 存储 loading Promise，`verifyProvider` 中 await 它，确保验证时 catalog 已就绪
- **重试机制**：`reloadModelCatalog()` 在 gateway ready 后自动重试，覆盖初始加载失败的场景
- **Provider 别名**：`PROVIDER_KEY_ALIASES` 映射 OneClaw 的 provider key 到 openclaw catalog key（如 `zai-cn` → `zai`）

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` 编译通过
- [x] `npm run dev` 启动，日志确认 `[model-catalog] loaded 801 models (616 unique)`
- [x] Gateway ready 后 catalog 自动重试成功
- [x] `resolveModelInput` fallback 逻辑验证：无信号→`["text"]`，explicit true→`["text","image"]`，explicit false→`["text"]`
- [x] Settings/Setup UI 中"图像支持"checkbox 已移除
- [ ] 用真实 API Key 验证 deepseek-chat 保存后 input 为 `["text"]`
- [ ] 用真实 API Key 验证图片模型保存后 input 为 `["text","image"]`

## Purpose

There is a preexisting pitfall in the weight-loading logic of `Qwen2MoTForCausalLM`: it uses `for...else` to try stacked param names first, then fall back to direct loading. However, when a stacked entry matches the weight name, but the fused param doesn't exist, the `break` skips the `else`, and the param is added to `loaded_params` while being empty. This was not an issue until #2490 tried to support LoRA on `gate_proj` and `up_proj`, and therefore added `gate_up_proj` into `stacked_params_mapping`. 

This PR uses an explicit `loaded` flag to detect the loading status and therefore ensures the default loading path always runs if the param is not loaded via the fused param. Fixes the issue and makes the loading more robust.

author: jarvisxyz
body:
## Summary

Fixes missing markdown → mrkdwn conversion in `edit_message()`, causing broken formatting and malformed URLs when editing messages.

## Problem

The `send()` method in the Slack adapter correctly converts standard markdown to Slack's `mrkdwn` format using `format_message()`. However, `edit_message()` was sending raw content directly to `chat_update`, skipping this conversion.

### Impact

- **Bold text**: `**text**` rendered literally instead of *text*
- **Links with formatting**: `[link](https://...)` in bold/context became `<https://...|link>**` with trailing `**` included in the clickable URL → 404 errors
- **Headers/code blocks**: Rendered with raw markdown syntax visible

This was discovered after PR #5558 links were unclickable due to trailing `**` from bold syntax becoming part of the URL.

## Solution

Added `format_message(content)` call in `edit_message()` before sending to `chat_update`, matching the behavior of `send()`.

```python
# Convert standard markdown → Slack mrkdwn
formatted = self.format_message(content)

await self._get_client(chat_id).chat_update(
    channel=chat_id,
    ts=message_id,
    text=formatted,  # Was: text=content
)
```

## Changes

- `gateway/platforms/slack.py`: Added `format_message()` call in `edit_message()`

## Testing

All 69 Slack gateway tests pass. The existing test suite validates the `format_message()` function; this fix ensures `edit_message()` uses it consistently with `send()`.

## Backwards Compatibility

Fully backwards compatible — only fixes broken behavior. Edited messages will now render correctly instead of showing raw markdown.

author: g3rmanaviator
body:
Summary

This PR upgrades the base image and adds optional Intel iGPU hardware-accelerated encoding via VAAPI.

### Changes

**Infrastructure**
- Upgraded base image from Ubuntu 22.04 to **Ubuntu 24.04**
- Upgraded Node.js to **v22**
- Updated audio library reference to `libasound2t64` (renamed in Ubuntu 24.04)
- Intel VAAPI driver stack (`intel-media-va-driver-non-free`, `libvpl2`, `libva2`, `libva-drm2`) now baked into the image on amd64

**New: Intel iGPU hardware encoding (`ENABLE_IGPU`)**
- When `ENABLE_IGPU=true`, FFmpeg uses `h264_vaapi` for encoding instead of `libx264`, offloading transcoding to the Intel iGPU
- Requires `--device=/dev/dri` passed to the container
- If the device is not found at startup, the container automatically falls back to CPU encoding (`libx264`) and logs a warning
- Container logs report the active transcoding mode on startup: `Transcoding mode: iGPU (h264_vaapi)` or `CPU (libx264)`

author: sv10p
body:
**Summary**
Implemented the complete auth flow: UI components, strict Zod validation, HTTP-only cookies, automatic token rotation, and fully typed GraphQL queries via codegen.

**Key Features & DX**

Type-Safe API (Codegen): Integrated GraphQL Code Generator (@/gqlcodegen). All auth mutations and queries are now strictly typed.

**Smart GraphQL Client:** Built a custom gqlRequest utility. It handles token rotation automatically (silent refresh) by intercepting UNAUTHENTICATED errors and updating tokens via Server Actions.

**Security First:** Tokens and user_id are now securely stored in httpOnly cookies with a lax SameSite policy.

**Form & Validation:** Unified Zod schemas for all auth forms. Next.js Server Actions encapsulate the core mutation logic.

**UI Kit & Tests:** Added accessible UI primitives (Radix UI + CVA), unit tests and full E2E Playwright coverage (including an automated test-user teardown).

**How to test**

Run the unit and E2E test suites to verify happy paths and edge cases.

**Session refresh test:** While logged in, manually delete or modify your access_token cookie, then trigger an action. The app should silently fetch a new token without logging you out.

author: haiyuazhang
body:
## Problem

New management plane TypeSpec projects can currently configure the legacy `@azure-tools/typespec-csharp` emitter for .NET SDK generation in their `tspconfig.yaml`. This emitter is being retired and should not be used for new management plane projects.

## Solution

Add a new **required** validation sub-rule `TspConfigCsharpMgmtEmitterRequiredSubRule` to the existing `SdkTspConfigValidation` rule in the TypeSpec Validation CI check.

### Rule behavior
- **Skips** for data-plane projects (only applies to `resource-manager/` paths)
- **Passes** if `@azure-typespec/http-client-csharp-mgmt` is found in the `emit` array or `options`
- **Fails** with specific guidance if legacy `@azure-tools/typespec-csharp` is configured instead
- **Fails** with onboarding guidance if no .NET emitter is configured at all

### Test coverage
Added 6 test cases covering:
- Valid config with emitter in `emit` array
- Valid config with emitter in `options`
- Failure when legacy emitter is in `emit`
- Failure when legacy emitter is in `options`
- Failure when no .NET emitter is configured
- Skip for data-plane projects

All 219 tests pass.

mongodb/node-mongodb-native (mongodb) ### [`v3.6.6`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/releases/tag/v3.6.6) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/compare/v3.6.5...v3.6.6) The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 3.6.6 of the driver #### Release Highlights This patch addresses a number of bugs listed below. The events generated from this client are forwarded to the client instance you initialize so it is possible to monitor all events. #### Bug - \[[NODE-2995](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-2995)] - Sharing a MongoClient for metadata lookup can lead to deadlock in drivers using automatic encryption - \[[NODE-3050](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3050)] - Infinite loop on Windows due to a bug in require\_optional package - \[[NODE-3120](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3120)] - TypeError: Cannot read property 'roundTripTime' of undefined - \[[NODE-3122](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3122)] - Pipelining an upload stream of GridFSBucket never finishes on Node v14 - \[[NODE-3129](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3129)] - Collection () .. .setReadPreference() not routing query to secondaries - \[[NODE-3133](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3133)] - autoEncryption produces serverHeartbeatFailed - with MongoError typemismatch #### Improvement - \[[NODE-3070](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3070)] - Define error handling behavior of writeErrors and writeConcernError on Mongos #### Documentation - Reference: - API: - Changelog: We invite you to try the driver immediately, and report any issues to the NODE project. Thanks very much to all the community members who contributed to this release! ### [`v3.6.5`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/releases/tag/v3.6.5) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/compare/v3.6.4...v3.6.5) The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 3.6.5 of the driver! #### Notable Fixes In this patch there is a fix surrounding an issue some users were encountering in serverless environments when using the Unified Topology. If the nodejs process went unused for a great amount of time there was an intermittent issue that would cause `startSession` to fail, however, issuing a dummy read request would resolve the problem. The session support check is now done after server selection meaning the driver has the most up to date information about the MongoDB deployment before utilizing sessions. We encourage any user's that implemented workarounds to updated their driver and make use of this fix. In addition, the previous release of our driver added a warning about an upcoming change in the v4 version of the driver about how users can specify their write concern options. We've updated the driver to use nodejs's `process.emitWarning` API in nearly all cases where the driver prints something out, as well as limit most warning messages to only be printed once. #### Bug - session support detection spec compliance ([#​2732](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/issues/2732)) ([9baec71](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/commit/9baec7128f612f2d9c290c85d24e33602f911499)) - \[[NODE-3100](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3100)] - startSession fails intermittently on servers that support sessions - \[[NODE-3066](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3066)] - Accessing non-existent property 'MongoError' of module exports inside circular dependency - \[[NODE-3114](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3114)] - Incorrect warning: Top-level use of w, wtimeout, j, and fsync is deprecated - \[[NODE-3119](https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/NODE-3119)] - Node 14.5.4, mongo 3.6.4 Circular warnings ### [`v3.6.4`](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/releases/tag/v3.6.4) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mongodb/node-mongodb-native/compare/v3.6.3...v3.6.4) ### MongoDB Driver v3.6.4 The MongoDB Node.js team is pleased to announce version 3.6.4 of the driver #### Release Highlights ##### Explain Support The full set of $explain verbosity settings are now supported: - `queryPlanner` - `queryPlannerExtended` - `executionStats` - `allPlansExecution` In the following commands: - `aggregate()` (MDB 3.0+) - `find()` (MDB 3.0+) - `remove()` (MDB 3.0+) - `update()` (MDB 3.0+) - `distinct()` (MDB 3.2+) - `findAndModify()` (MDB 3.2+) - `mapReduce()` (MDB 4.4+) You can get a lot of insight into the performance of a query or optimization using these fine grained reports. To learn more about how to use explain [read here](https://docs.mongodb.com/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain/). ##### Direct Connection Issue Revert We removed automatic direct connection for the unified topology in the 3.6.3 release of the driver. This change was preparatory for the 4.0 version of the driver, where we'll always perform automatic discovery. To avoid making this kind of change in a patch release, this version restores automatic direct connection when connecting to a single host using the unified topology without a specified replicaSet and without directConnection: false, in line with previous 3.6 releases. > **NOTE:** In the next major version the `unifiedTopology` is the only Topology and it is required to either specify a `replicaSet` name or enable `directConnection` in order to connect to single nodes

body:
The doctor orchestrator had two silent failure modes: (1) passing an invalid tier name (e.g. run_doctor(tier='foo')) silently returned a healthy report with zero checks, giving false confidence that the system was healthy; (2) if any tier's provider raised an unhandled exception, the entire run_doctor call crashed instead of degrading gracefully — meaning a bug in one tier's checks could prevent all diagnostic output.

Summary:
Added input validation for the tier parameter — invalid tiers now produce a critical-status report with a clear error check instead of an empty healthy report. Wrapped each tier runner in try/except so that if a provider crashes, the orchestrator captures the exception as a critical DoctorCheck (with traceback evidence) and continues running remaining tiers. This ensures partial diagnostic results are always available even when one tier is broken. Added 3 new tests: invalid tier detection, single-tier crash capture, and partial crash with cross-tier preservation.

## Summary

When a wallet transaction's unconfirmed inputs reference an aggregate mempool ancestor set whose size exceeds the `GatherClusters()` DoS limit (currently 500), `MiniMiner` cannot compute combined bump fees and `CreateRateBumpTransaction()` must surface a clear error to the caller instead of crashing or silently returning garbage.

This adds a unit test that constructs the offending topology, eight disjoint mempool chains, each at the cluster-count cap, totalling 512 transactions, and exercises `CreateRateBumpTransaction` through a wallet tx whose inputs are the chain tips. The construction is parameterised on `MAX_CLUSTER_COUNT_LIMIT` and the local `kGatherClustersDoSLimit`, so it survives changes to either; a `static_assert` pins the relationship at compile time. author: git-on-my-level
body:
## Summary
- route `GitHubService` CLI execution through a shared `GitHubCliBroker` backed by global `.codex-autorunner` state
- share cached `gh api rate_limit` responses and a cross-process cooldown after rate-limit hits so later callers fail fast instead of stampeding `gh`
- tag polling traffic through the shared broker and keep idle GitHub discovery on an explicit low-frequency budget

## Why
`gh` usage was centralized only at a per-instance wrapper, so separate services and pollers still behaved like independent clients. That made it hard to apply global backoff or shared quota decisions, and the idle polling path could keep consuming GitHub budget even when nothing was happening.

## Impact
Interactive GitHub features still use the existing `GitHubService` surface, but they now inherit shared broker behavior automatically. Polling traffic also runs through the same broker, which gives the codebase one place to add future caching, prioritization, and smarter rate-limit handling.

## Validation

Replaces the hardcoded core-only coverage step with dynamic, incremental coverage for all PR-affected modules.

author: gabrielima7
body:
**Severity:** HIGH

**Vulnerability:**
1. **Unbounded URL Parsing (CWE-400):** URL parsing logic lacked a maximum length check, exposing the system to Denial of Service via resource exhaustion from massive inputs.
2. **SSRF Bypass via URL Parsing (CWE-918):** Domain extraction relied on manually splitting `parsed.netloc`, which can be bypassed using credentials or IPv6 structures, bypassing SSRF validators.
3. **Weak JWT Signatures:** The application lacked validation for the length of HMAC keys used for signing JWTs, leading to vulnerabilities if short secrets were provided.

**Impact:**
- Attackers could degrade system performance through resource exhaustion during URL parsing.
- Malicious actors could bypass SSRF protections, enabling internal network scanning or data exfiltration.
- Weak JWT secrets could be brute-forced, compromising authentication logic.

**Fix:**
- Added `MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048` to strictly bound URL sizes prior to parsing.
- Refactored `validators.py` to use `parsed.hostname` instead of `netloc.split(":")[0]`.
- Refactored `guards.py` to explicitly enforce the URL max length check.
- Added byte-length validation in `jwt.py` to ensure HMAC keys meet the 32-byte (256-bit) minimum security standard.
- Introduced two new custom Semgrep rules (`taipanstack.security-url-max-length`, `taipanstack.security-insecure-netloc-split`) to prevent regressions.

**Verification:**
- Ran the full test suite via `poetry run pytest` (1165 tests passed).
- Executed the custom Semgrep ruleset via `poetry run semgrep --config .semgrep/taipanstack-rules.yml src/taipanstack/`, which returned 0 findings.

author: jonmcwest
body:
## Problem

Logs alert users need a way to validate their alert configurations before deploying them to production. Without simulation capabilities, users must rely on trial-and-error to tune thresholds, evaluation windows, and N-of-M settings, potentially leading to alert fatigue or missed incidents.

## Changes  
![image.png](https://app.graphite.com/user-attachments/assets/d36dc7c7-eafb-4380-8905-c4ffd3eb4b49.png)

![image.png](https://app.graphite.com/user-attachments/assets/596203a9-f3d1-4542-b97e-b9addc529249.png)

Added a comprehensive alert simulation feature that allows users to test their logs alert configurations against historical data:

**Backend Changes:**

- Added `/simulate/` endpoint to the logs alerts API that runs the full alert state machine against historical data
- Implemented `_fill_empty_buckets()` to handle sparse ClickHouse results by filling gaps with zero-count entries
- Added rolling window calculation to simulate real alerting behavior (check every minute, count logs in the last N minutes)
- Extracted `_validate_filters()` for shared validation between create/update and simulate operations
- Added comprehensive serializers for simulation request/response with proper validation

**Frontend Changes:**

- Created `LogsAlertSimulation` component with interactive chart visualization using Chart.js
- Added incident extraction and summary statistics (total alerts, firing time, resolutions)
- Implemented detailed incident table showing start time, duration, peak counts, and resolution status
- Added simulation controls with time range selection (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
- Integrated simulation modal accessible via "Simulate" button in alert form
- Added real-time form synchronization that clears simulation results when alert settings change

**Key Features:**

- Full state machine evaluation including N-of-M logic and cooldown periods
- Visual chart with color-coded bars (normal/breached/fired) and threshold line
- Human-readable explanations for each state transition
- Comprehensive validation matching the main alert creation flow

## How did you test this code?

Added extensive unit tests covering:

- Basic simulation response structure validation
- Rolling window calculation with sparse data
- N-of-M evaluation logic with delayed firing
- Cooldown suppression of repeat notifications
- Empty results handling
- Input validation for filters, windows, and N-of-M parameters
- Threshold configuration echo in response

The tests use mocked `AlertCheckQuery` results and `freeze_time` to ensure deterministic behavior. Frontend integration tested through the existing alert form workflow.

body:
## Problem

The livestream service connects to Warpstream without AZ awareness because there's no way to configure the Kafka `client.id` per consumer, which Warpstream uses for routing traffic to agents in the same availability zone.

## Changes

- Add a `ClientID` field to `ConsumerConfig` so each consumer (event, session recording, notification) can have its own `client.id`
- Bind per-consumer env vars: `LIVESTREAM_CONSUMERS_EVENT_CLIENT_ID`, `LIVESTREAM_CONSUMERS_SESSION_RECORDING_CLIENT_ID`, `LIVESTREAM_CONSUMERS_NOTIFICATION_CLIENT_ID`
- Apply `client.id` in `applyKafkaConfigOverrides`, which all three consumers already call


## How did you test this code?

author: makdia
body:
## What does this PR do and why?

In Elementor's editor context, `ProductInfoWidget::render()` was calling `AssetLoader::loadSingleProductAssets()` which enqueues frontend JS. This caused Elementor to re-render the widget unexpectedly, creating a feedback loop in the editor panel. Additionally, `renderDescription()` runs through `the_content` filter, which Elementor hooks into — triggering it inside the editor caused re-entry issues.

The `product-select-control.js` was firing the generic `change` event on the Select2 control after loading a pre-selected product, which could trigger unintended event listeners beyond Select2 itself.

## Changes

**PHP**
- Detect editor context via `\Elementor\Plugin::$instance->editor->is_edit_mode()` — `ProductInfoWidget.php:337`
- In editor: skip `loadSingleProductAssets()`, only enqueue CSS — `ProductInfoWidget.php:339-347`
- In editor: render description directly via `wpautop($post->post_content)` wrapped in `wp_kses_post()` instead of going through `renderDescription()` / `the_content` filter — `ProductInfoWidget.php:400-408`

**JS**
- Change `$select.trigger('change')` → `$select.trigger('change.select2')` to scope the trigger to Select2's own handler only — `product-select-control.js:145`

## How to test

1. Open a FluentCart product template in Elementor Theme Builder with a Product Info widget placed
2. Verify the widget renders the product correctly in the editor without flickering or re-rendering
3. Verify the product description renders in the editor preview
4. Toggle **Description** off in the widget settings → verify it disappears in the editor
5. Open the Elementor editor on any page with the product select control — select a product and verify no console errors or double-trigger side effects
6. On the frontend (not editor), verify the full product info still renders correctly including JS-powered elements (variation select, add to cart)

## Anything the reviewer should know?

The editor path for description intentionally bypasses `the_content` filter and uses `wpautop()` directly — this is safe since we're only rendering in the Elementor preview iframe, not saving or outputting to a public page. The frontend path is unchanged and continues to use `renderDescription()`.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The `POST /api/provision/signup` endpoint was failing with a 500 because `from app.sanitize import sanitize_text as sanitize` was placed inside the `agent_signup` function body rather than at the module level. While Python allows deferred imports, placing it inside an async handler means any import resolution error surfaces as a runtime 500 on every request rather than a startup-time failure, and it also re-executes the import machinery on every signup call.

## Solution

Moved `from app.sanitize import sanitize_text as sanitize` to the module-level import block alongside the other `app.*` imports, and removed the now-redundant in-function import. The function `sanitize_text` already exists in `app/sanitize.py` with the correct signature, so the import resolves cleanly at module load time and the signup endpoint works as expected.

### Changes
- **Modified** `app/routes/provision.py`

author: maksp86
body:
### Motivation

- Reduce memory and port exhaustion when converting and probing large numbers of proxy links by processing in chunks. 
- Ensure deterministic selection of top-N candidates by latency while avoiding full-list sorts for large inputs. 
- Avoid collisions on inbound SOCKS ports when running many concurrent Xray instances by using a managed port pool and overriding inbound ports per runtime.

### Description

- Introduces chunked processing helpers ` _chunked` and `_chunked_candidates` and uses them in `ProxyProbe.url_test_batch`, `ProxyProbe.speed_test_batch`, and pipeline link conversion workflows to process inputs in manageable batches. 
- Adds a port pool strategy (`PORT_POOL_START` and an asyncio `Queue`) and per-run SOCKS port overriding via `_override_socks_port` to avoid port conflicts across concurrent Xray instances, and updates `_url_test_candidate` and `_speed_test_candidate` to accept a `socks_port`. 
- Replaces the previous global `start_port`/port-limited batching in `XrayToolchain.convert_links` with `_build_link_batches` driven by a `chunk_size` parameter and removes `start_port` usage from public API and internal converter invocation. 
- Implements a memory-friendly stable top-N selection for latency using a max-heap with `_add_top_latency_row` and `_latency_value` to keep best candidates without sorting entire lists, and updates the pipeline to stream URL results into that heap. 
- Adjusts URL post-processing helper `_collect_url_stage_rows` signature to accept a minimal `by_hash_link` mapping and tolerate missing entries, and refactors related call sites. 

### Testing

- Ran the project unit test suite with `pytest` and observed all tests passing. 
- Performed a local integration smoke test of the probe pipeline by invoking `run_once` with a small sample `AppConfig` and a local `XrayToolchain`, which completed the URL and speed stages without runtime port conflicts.

author: delano
body:
## Summary

Invite signups no longer require a separate email verification step — the invite link itself proves email ownership. After signing up via an invite link, users are automatically verified and logged in.

- Auto-verify accounts at both SQL and Redis layers when a valid invite is accepted during signup
- Auto-login via Rodauth's `create_account_autologin?` gate, coordinated with an `@invite_accepted` flag
- Redesign the email mismatch screen: neutral "Different account signed in" tone replaces the alarmist "Wrong Account" warning, with a "Continue as {email}" action that logs out and returns to the invite page
- Suppress the verification email only for validated invite tokens — not based on the raw request param

## Security fixes

The initial implementation suppressed the verification email based on an unvalidated `request.params['invite_token']`. An attacker could add `invite_token=garbage` to any signup form to suppress the email, enabling email squatting. Three fixes applied:

- **Token validation in `send_verify_account_email`**: Now looks up the invitation and checks it's pending, not expired, and email-bound before suppressing. Garbage tokens fall through to normal verification.
- **`update_account` instead of direct SQL**: Keeps Rodauth's in-memory account hash in sync with the DB after status change.
- **Flag ordering**: `@invite_accepted = true` moved after DB operations so autologin only fires if verification actually succeeded.

## Test plan

- [x] 34 existing tryouts tests pass (invite acceptance, email mismatch, verified_by audit trail)
- [x] 26 new security regression tests (garbage token gate, expired/mismatch token handling, flag safety on DB failure)
- [ ] E2E: `npx playwright test invite-flow-states` — 6-state invite flow machine
- [ ] E2E: `npx playwright test org-invitation-flow` — full invitation journey
- [ ] E2E: `npx playwright test invitation-email-mismatch` — mismatch UX
- [ ] Manual: signup with `?invite_token=garbage` shows verification-pending state, not auto-login

Closes #2916

author: copilot
body:
Three independent gameplay bugs: driver has no joystick on mobile, gunner's rapid fire never stops once triggered, and the concussive blast cooldown is too slow.

## Changes

- **Mobile joystick (`public/controls.js` lines 107, 157):** Guard clauses were inverted — they returned early when both menus were *hidden* (i.e., during gameplay), preventing joystick initialization entirely. Flipped to bail when either menu is *visible*:
  ```js
  // Before — exits during active match
  if (start.hidden && lobby.hidden) return;
  // After — exits during menus
  if (!start.hidden || !lobby.hidden) return;
  ```

- **Rapid-fire latch (`game-engine.js` line 79):** Server only ever assigned `true` to `triggerSecondary`, so once fired it stayed latched regardless of client input. Changed to a full boolean sync:
  ```js
  // Before
  if (input.triggerSecondary) tank.gunnerInputs.triggerSecondary = true;
  // After
  tank.gunnerInputs.triggerSecondary = Boolean(input.triggerSecondary);
  ```

- **Cannon cooldown (`driver.js` + `public/app.js`):** Halved cooldown from `2.5s` → `1.25s` and updated the HUD ring percentage divisor to match.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

There are three bugs to fix:

## Bug 1: Driver joystick doesn't work on mobile

In `public/controls.js`, the `setupTouchControls` method has a guard clause on line 107 that returns early if both the start screen AND lobby screen are hidden (meaning the match is active). This prevents the touch joystick from being set up during gameplay.

The problem is this line (107):
```js
if(document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.contains('hidden') && document.getElementById('lobby-screen').classList.contains('hidden')) return;
```

This check causes the `touchstart` handler to completely bail out when the game is in progress. The joystick initialization code (lines 145-148) never runs during the match, so the driver has no way to move on mobile.

**Fix:** Invert the logic — the joystick touch code should only run when the match IS active (both screens hidden). The early return should happen when the start/lobby screens are SHOWING, not when they're hidden. The correct guard should be:
```js
if(!document.getElementById('start-screen').classList.contains('hidden') || !document.getElementById('lobby-screen').classList.contains('hidden')) return;
```

Apply the same fix to the similar guard on line 157 in the `touchmove` handler.

## Bug 2: Rapid fire (secondary weapon) never stops shooting

In `public/controls.js`, line 266, the gunner's secondary fire input is set based on whether the button is *held down*:
```js
this.input.triggerSecondary = Boolean(this.touchBtns.jump || this.keys['ShiftLeft'] || this.keys['ShiftRight']);
```

However, `triggerSecondary` is meant to be a one-shot trigger. Looking at `game-engine.js` line 79, on the server the `triggerSecondary` flag is set to `true` when received and never gets cleared by the server — the server only uses it to fire, but doesn't reset it. The flag IS reset on the client side in `network.js` line 42 (`window.Controls.input.triggerSecondary = false`), but because `processKeyboard()` runs every frame and continuously sets `triggerSecondary = true` while the button is held, and the input sync only runs at 30fps, the flag is basically always `true` while the button is held.

The real problem is on the **server side** in `game-engine.js` line 79:
```js
if (input.triggerSecondary) tank.gunnerInputs.triggerSecondary = true;
```

The server sets it to `true` but never resets it to `false`. So once the player presses the secondary fire button, the tank keeps shooting rapid fire rounds forever, even after releasing the button.

**Fix:** In `game-engine.js`, in the `applyInput` method, change line 79 to properly sync the value instead of only ever setting it to true. It should also set it to `false` when the input is `false`:
```js
tank.gunnerInputs.triggerSecondary = Boolean(input.triggerSecondary);
```

## Bug 3: Cannon (concussive blast) should fire faster — halve the cooldown

In `driver.js`, line 97, the concussive blast cooldown is set to 2.5 seconds:
```js
this.bombCooldown = 2.5;
```

The user says the cannon should be "a little faster. Half the time probably."

**Fix:** Change the cooldown from `2.5` to `1.25` in `driver.js` line 97. Also update the HUD percentage calculation in `public/app.js` line 316 where it divides by `2.5` — change it to divide by `1.25`:
```js
pct = Math.max(0, 1 - sp.bombCooldown / 1.25);
```


The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: The driver can't move in this game on mobile. There is no joystick. Also the gunner, when the rapid fire shoots, it doesn't ever stop? And the cannon should be a little faster. Half the time probably

Assistant: 

Let me investigate the codebase to understand the current game mechanics and find the relevant files.

Assistant: Now I have a complete understanding of the three bugs. Let me create a PR to fix all of them.

Assistant: I've kicked off a PR to fix all three issues. Here's a summary of what was found and what's being changed:

### 🐛 Bug 1: Driver joystick broken on mobile
In `public/controls.js`, the `touchstart` and `touchmove` handlers have a guard clause that accidentally returns early **during gameplay** (when both start-screen and lobby-screen are hidden). This prevents the joystick from ever working in a match on mobile. The fix inverts the logic so the joystick code runs when the game *is* active, and bails out when menus are still showing.

### 🐛 Bug 2: Rapid fire never stops
In `game-engine.js` line 79, the server does:
```js
if (input.triggerSecondary) tank.gunnerInputs.triggerSecondary = true;
```
This only ever sets the flag to `true` — it never resets to `false`. Once triggered, the rapid fire shoots forever. The fix changes this to properly sync the boolean value in both directions: `tank.gunnerInputs.triggerSecondary = Boolean(input.triggerSecondary);`

### 🐛 Bug 3: Cannon too slow
The concussive blast cooldown in `driver.js` is `2.5` seconds. Per your request ("half the time"), it's being changed to `1.25` seconds...

</details>

body:
## Description

Add a clap-based CLI with four subcommands (`run`, `validate`, `reload`, `version`) while preserving full backwards compatibility — no-args invocation uses the existing env-var-only startup path unchanged. Smart path defaults and mode inference make `ferrum-edge run` work zero-config when local config files exist.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Test improvement

## Changes Made

- **`src/cli.rs`** — New module: clap derive structs (`Cli`, `Command`, `RunArgs`, `ValidateArgs`, `ReloadArgs`, `VersionArgs`), smart path resolution for settings/spec files, `apply_run_overrides()`/`apply_validate_overrides()` that inject CLI flags as env vars before config loading, `execute_validate()` for config checking, `execute_reload()` for SIGHUP dispatch, `execute_version()` for version output
- **`src/main.rs`** — Integrated CLI parsing at the top of `main()` before `CONF_FILE_CACHE` OnceLock initialization. Early-exit for `version`/`reload`, override injection for `run`/`validate`, validate exit after crypto+logging init
- **`src/lib.rs`** — Exported `cli` module for test access
- **`build.rs`** — Emit `TARGET` env var for `version --json` output
- **`Cargo.toml`** — Added `clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }`
- **`docs/cli.md`** — Full CLI reference: all subcommands, options, examples, precedence rules, smart defaults, backwards compatibility
- **`README.md`** — Added CLI examples to Getting Started section
- **`FEATURES.md`** — Added CLI feature section
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — Added CLI subcommands to Quick Reference, `cli.rs` to Source Layout, updated Startup Sequence

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests pass (`cargo test --test unit_tests`) — 2,779 passed
- [x] Integration tests pass (`cargo test --test integration_tests`) — 154 passed
- [x] E2E tests pass (`cargo test --test functional_tests -- --ignored functional_cli`) — 12 passed
- [x] Clippy passes with zero warnings (`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`)
- [x] Code is formatted (`cargo fmt --check`)

### Test Cases

1. **28 unit tests** (`tests/unit/cli/cli_tests.rs`): clap parsing (no args, version, run with all options, short flags, verbose levels, validate, reload), smart path resolution (absolute, relative, env var precedence, local file discovery), `apply_run_overrides` (mode setting, verbose levels, spec→file inference, explicit mode preservation), `apply_validate_overrides`, `execute_version` smoke, `execute_reload` error handling
2. **12 functional tests** (`tests/functional/functional_cli_test.rs`): `version` / `version --json` output, `--help` / `run --help` subcommand listing, `validate` with valid spec / nonexistent spec / invalid YAML / with settings, `run` starts+stops+health-check, `run -v` verbose, `reload --pid` sends SIGHUP to running gateway, no-args legacy mode backwards compatibility

## Checklist

- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly (if applicable)
- [x] My changes don't introduce new clippy warnings
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have checked that my changes don't break backward compatibility

## Performance Impact

- [x] No performance impact

CLI parsing runs once at startup before any hot path. The `clap` dependency adds ~200-400KB to the binary, negligible given the existing dependency tree.

## Additional Notes

**Configuration precedence**: CLI flag > env var > conf file > smart path defaults > hardcoded defaults. CLI flags are translated to env vars via `unsafe { std::env::set_var() }` in the single-threaded startup context (same pattern as existing secret resolution), then the existing `EnvConfig` chain handles everything.

**Smart path defaults search order**:
- Settings: `./ferrum.conf` → `./config/ferrum.conf` → `/etc/ferrum/ferrum.conf`
- Spec: `./resources.yaml` → `./resources.json` → `./config/resources.yaml` → `./config/resources.json` → `/etc/ferrum/config.yaml` → `/etc/ferrum/config.json`

author: ninenox
body:
## Summary

Fixes end-to-end token usage tracking — counts were not being recorded for streaming providers and the webchat UI always showed `—`.

**Three bugs fixed:**

- **`openai.rs`** — Add `stream_options: { "include_usage": true }` to streaming requests. Without this flag, OpenAI-compatible APIs (vLLM, OpenAI) omit the `usage` field from SSE chunks entirely, so `accumulate_usage` was never called for any streaming turn.
- **`router.rs`** — Move `GET /api/usage` from API-key-protected routes to public routes. When `api_key: null` (default), the middleware returns 403, making the endpoint unreachable from the webchat UI.
- **`main.js`** — Use period-only query (no `session_id`) so the UI shows global cross-session usage, matching the intent of the period dropdown (All time / Today / Last 7 days / Last 30 days). Add `cache: "no-store"` to prevent stale counts when switching periods.

**Also fix `runtime.rs`**: the streaming path passed `""` as model name to `accumulate_usage`. Now uses `provider.configured_model()` so the correct model name (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`) is stored in `usage_log` for all streaming providers.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check && cargo test --workspace && cargo clippy && cargo fmt --check` all pass
- [x] vLLM streaming: final SSE chunk now includes `usage` → input/output tokens recorded
- [x] `GET /api/usage` accessible without API key when `api_key: null`
- [x] Webchat UI shows correct global token counts — same value across all browser windows
- [x] Period filter works correctly (verified via SQLite: `date(recorded_at) = date('now')` filters as expected)
- [x] `cache: "no-store"` prevents stale browser cache when switching periods
- [x] Verified via SQLite: `usage_log` records model name, provider, and token counts correctly
- [x] Non-streaming providers (Ollama, LINE, WeChat, etc.) unaffected

### Changes proposed in this Pull Request:

Bots enumerating filter combos (e.g. `filter_color=red,blue` vs `blue,red`) generate separate cache entries for logically identical queries.

Adds `FilterData::normalize_query_vars()` called before hashing in both `get_transient_key()` and `get_cached_product_ids()`. Original `$query_vars` are never mutated — normalisation is on a copy used only for the key.

Rules: `ksort` all keys; sort/trim/lowercase comma values for `filter_*`, `rating_filter`, `categories`, `tags`, `brands`; lowercase `query_type_*`; trim `min_price`/`max_price`.

2. Reload with filters reversed (Blue + Red).
3. Both requests should hit the same transient key.
4. Repeat with category/tag filters to verify taxonomy params are also normalised.

author: mitnitsky
body:
## Summary

On macOS with `LSUIElement=true`, Flameshot runs as an agent app with no dock icon. This makes it impossible to Cmd+Tab to open windows or see the app in the dock.

This PR adds a dock icon that appears while any user-facing window is visible and disappears when the last one is closed or hidden.

## Supported windows

- Settings (ConfigWindow)
- About (InfoWindow)
- Capture Launcher (CaptureLauncher)
- Upload History (UploadHistory)

## Implementation

- `Flameshot::showDockIcon(QWidget*)` — public one-liner for any window. Call after `show()`.
- Uses `QWindow::visibilityChanged` signal to track window visibility.
- Per-window dynamic property (`_visibleInDock`) prevents double-counting on minimize/maximize transitions.
- Reference counter toggles `NSApplicationActivationPolicy` between Regular (dock icon) and Accessory (no dock icon).
- Adding a new window requires just one line: `showDockIcon(myWidget)`.

## Testing

Tested on macOS 26.4 (Tahoe), Apple Silicon, Qt 6.11.0:
- Open/close each window type — dock icon appears/disappears correctly
- Multiple windows open — dock icon stays until last one closes
- CaptureLauncher hide (start capture) + close settings — dock icon disappears
- Minimize/restore — dock icon persists correctly

author: fairchild
body:
## Re-ship of #311 (innocent victim of misattribution)

PR #311 shipped tmux-in-sandbox for real Resume continuity. Immediately after deploy, the dashboard hierarchy went down with SSR exceptions. I assumed #311 caused it and reverted in #312. The revert didn't help — the dashboard stayed down.

Diagnostic endpoint #313 revealed the actual root cause: **Turso row-read quota exceeded**. Nothing to do with tmux. The quota had been building up for weeks from a missing composite index on webhook_events (fixed in #314).

This PR re-applies #311 verbatim. It's a clean revert-of-the-revert — same code as #311, no changes. Should be safe to merge now that the DB is healthy and the root cause is actually fixed.

## What the change does (copied from #311)

Makes \"Resume\" actually mean \"land where you left off.\"

Before: Resume restored the Vercel sandbox snapshot (filesystem) but bash was a fresh process. Users saw files come back but \`cd\`, env vars, command history, in-flight processes were gone.

After: ttyd runs \`tmux new-session -A -s shell\` instead of bare bash. Because tmux persists session state to disk, and disk is part of the Vercel snapshot, the shell process itself survives the snapshot/restore round-trip.

Three coordinated changes:
1. \`BASE_SNAPSHOT_VERSION\` bumped \`v2-ttyd\` → \`v3-tmux\` (new base snapshot built on first request)
2. \`resolveBaseSnapshot\` installs tmux alongside ttyd: \`apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tmux\`
3. \`startTtyd\` command changed from \`bash\` to \`tmux new-session -A -s shell\`

One-place change because of the \`startTtyd\` extraction from #305 — all three sandbox creation paths pick up tmux automatically.

## Test plan

- [x] \`mise run web:check\` — 103/103 unit, lint + typecheck clean
- [ ] Post-deploy: start a terminal, \`cd /tmp && export FOO=bar\`, snapshot + pause via the UI, Resume, verify \`pwd\` = \`/tmp\` and \`echo \$FOO\` = \`bar\`
- [ ] Monitor \`turso db inspect\` for any read-rate regression (expected: none — tmux doesn't touch the DB)

## Related

- #311 — original tmux PR (merged, then reverted)
- #312 — the unnecessary revert
- #313 — diagnostic endpoint that identified the real cause
- #314 — the actual fix (composite index + getEventStats cache + poll bump)

author: smart-ink
body:
### Motivation
- Create a lean internal monorepo MVP that converts ChatGPT export data into searchable memory and lightweight operational objects while keeping MemPalace behind a swappable adapter boundary. 
- Provide a practical import pipeline that normalizes conversations, chunks text, indexes memory, and surfaces extractable review candidates (prompts, tasks, meetings, decisions, assets, ideas). 
- Keep the product focused and minimal for internal ops workflows with clear source traceability and a fast review/approval flow. 
- Isolate environment-specific MemPalace integration behind a small adapter so the memory engine can be swapped later. 

### Description
- Scaffolded a pnpm/turbo monorepo with `apps/web`, `packages/{db,shared,ai}`, and `services/{ingest,memory,worker}`, plus `docs`, `Docker Compose`, and `.env.example`. 
- Implemented a full Prisma schema (`packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`) covering the requested models (Project, ChatSource, ChatConversation, ChatMessage, ChatChunk, InboxItem, SourceReference, Prompt, PromptRun, Task, Meeting, MeetingDecision, MeetingAction, Asset, AssetUsage, Idea, Decision, MemoryHit, AnalyticsSnapshot) and added a seed script (`packages/db/prisma/seed.ts`). 
- Built the Python ingestion service (`services/ingest`) that implements `parse_chatgpt_export` → `normalize_transcript` → `chunk_message` → `extract_candidates`, persists `ChatSource`/`ChatConversation`/`ChatMessage`/`ChatChunk`/`InboxItem`/`SourceReference` and posts normalized chunks to the memory service. 
- Provided a memory service (`services/memory`) exposing an explicit adapter boundary with `index_conversation_chunks(...)` and `search_memory(...)` implemented as a local in-memory placeholder and documented TODOs to wire the real MemPalace runtime in `services/memory/src/adapter.py`. 
- Implemented the Next.js web app (`apps/web`) with the left-sidebar shell and MVP modules (Dashboard, Memory search, Prompt library, Tasks, Meetings, Review inbox, Assets, Analytics), plus API routes for `POST /api/import`, `POST /api/memory/search`, `GET /api/inbox`, and `POST /api/inbox/:id/approve` which maps inbox candidates into canonical objects on approval. 
- Added supporting artifacts: `docker-compose.yml` for local infra, sample ChatGPT export (`scripts/sample-chatgpt-export.json`), docs (`docs/*.md`), and a pre-coding implementation plan (`docs/implementation-plan.md`). 

### Testing
- Ran the ingestion unit tests with `cd services/ingest && pytest -q` which completed successfully (`5 passed`). 
- Performed Python syntax checks with `python -m py_compile services/ingest/src/*.py services/memory/src/*.py services/worker/src/*.py` which succeeded. 
- The MemPalace adapter is intentionally a placeholder for local MVP and includes `TODO(environment-specific)` markers in `services/memory/src/adapter.py` for the runtime integration steps.

author: rajashekar
body:
### 💡 What
Optimized the string parsing in the DuckDuckGo search provider. Instead of iterating over references and repeatedly cloning string slices (e.g., `result.text[..dash_pos].to_string()`), the loop now uses `.into_iter()` to consume the `DuckDuckGoResponse`. It takes ownership of the string and uses `split_off` and `truncate` to split it into a title and snippet.

### 🎯 Why
Extracting a prefix and suffix from an existing string by creating new `String` objects from sub-slices triggers two separate heap allocations. By consuming the struct and mutating the string in-place using `split_off()` and `truncate()`, we reuse the original heap buffer capacity for the prefix (title) and only perform one allocation for the new suffix (snippet). This minimizes memory overhead during large result parsing.

### 📊 Impact
Reduces string heap allocations per parsed DuckDuckGo search result by roughly 50-60%.

### 🔬 Measurement
Run `cargo check`, `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and the complete test suite:
`cargo test --features "pdf,unix-sockets,s3-sync"`
Verified all test cases passed locally in the sandboxed environment.
