author: mikejgray
body:
## Summary

Refactors the skill to delegate all OS-specific work to a controller selected at runtime by `sys.platform`. Brings macOS support over from [`OscillateLabsLLC/skill-mac-application-launcher`](https://github.com/OscillateLabsLLC/skill-mac-application-launcher) and leaves a clean hook for a future Windows contribution.

The skill class becomes pure orchestration; platform-specific code lives entirely in `controllers/{linux,macos,windows}.py`.

## Architecture

```
ovos_skill_application_launcher/
├── __init__.py              # Skill class — pure orchestration
└── controllers/
    ├── __init__.py          # get_controller() factory
    ├── base.py              # ApplicationController abstract base
    ├── linux.py             # .desktop files + wmctrl + psutil
    ├── macos.py             # .app bundles + AppleScript + open
    └── windows.py           # NotImplementedError stub with design notes
```

- **`controllers/base.py`** defines the abstract interface: `app_aliases`, `launch_app`, `close_app`, `is_running` are required; `can_switch_windows`, `switch_to_app`, `match_process`, `refresh_app_cache` are optional with safe defaults.
- **`controllers/linux.py`** is a verbatim refactor of the existing Linux logic (`.desktop` files, `wmctrl`, `psutil`) — **no behaviour changes**, just moved into a class.
- **`controllers/macos.py`** is the controller from the macOS fork: `.app` bundle parsing via `plistlib`, AppleScript via `osascript` for window switching and graceful quit, `open` / `open -a` for launching, `psutil` process matching as a fallback. Discovers apps from `/Applications`, `/System/Applications`, `/Applications/Utilities`, `/System/Library/CoreServices`, `~/Applications`.
- **`controllers/windows.py`** is a stub that raises `NotImplementedError` with a design sketch in the module docstring (registry-based discovery via `App Paths`, `Get-StartApps` via PowerShell, `os.startfile` / `subprocess.Popen` for launch, optional `pygetwindow`/`pywin32` for window management). A future contributor can fill this in without re-architecting the skill.
- **`controllers/__init__.py`** exposes `get_controller(settings, native_langs)` which dispatches on `sys.platform` and accepts a `controller_override` setting for testing or unusual environments.

## Backward compatibility

The historical public methods on `ApplicationLauncherSkill` are preserved as thin delegates so any third-party caller that did `from ovos_skill_application_launcher import ApplicationLauncherSkill` and called `parse_desktop_file`, `get_desktop_apps`, `match_window`, `close_by_window`, `close_by_process`, `match_process`, `switch_window`, `close_window`, `applist`, or `wmctrl` continues to work:

- The static methods (`parse_desktop_file`, `get_desktop_apps`) delegate to `LinuxApplicationController` because Linux remains the canonical implementation for the legacy public API.
- The instance methods delegate to whichever controller is active on the host OS.

## Tests

Adds **24 unit tests** in `test/test_controllers.py` and **2 e2e scaffold tests** in `test/end2end/test_launch_intent.py`, matching the OVOS singular-`test/` convention used by the existing CI workflows.

**Unit coverage:**
- Factory dispatch — `linux`, `linux2`, `darwin`, `macos`, `win32`, unknown fallback, `native_langs` threading, `controller_override` escape hatch
- Abstract base contract — cannot instantiate directly, default methods are safe no-ops
- Linux launch/close — `subprocess.Popen` mocked, threshold cutoff
- macOS launch — `open` vs `open -a` for paths vs bare names
- macOS AppleScript — activate/quit codepaths with `subprocess.run` mocked
- macOS `.app` bundle parsing — missing plist, full metadata, directory-name fallback
- Windows stub raises `NotImplementedError`

All unit tests run on any platform; OS-specific calls are mocked. **24/24 unit + 1 e2e import smoke passing locally, 1 e2e marked skip pending a launch_app monkeypatch (documented in the module docstring).**

## Manual verification on macOS

```text
controller class: MacOSApplicationController
applist len: 252
can_switch_windows: True
parse_desktop_file is static: True
```

End-to-end real Mac integration works: factory selected the right controller, discovered 252 real `.app` bundles, `can_switch_windows()` reports True (`osascript` present), and the legacy `ApplicationLauncherSkill.parse_desktop_file` is still callable.

## setup.py

Adds the new subpackage cleanly under the existing root-layout pattern:

```python
package_dir = {
    SKILL_PKG: \"\",
    "{SKILL_PKG}.controllers\": \"controllers\",
}
packages = [SKILL_PKG, "{SKILL_PKG}.controllers\"]
```

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest test/` — 25 passing, 1 skipped, covers all three controllers
- [x] Manual smoke test on macOS confirms real-world `.app` discovery and the factory dispatch
- [ ] CI on Linux runner
- [ ] Manual smoke test on Linux (someone with a Linux box, ideally with `wmctrl` present)

## Out of scope

- Windows implementation (intentionally a stub — see `controllers/windows.py` docstring for the design sketch)
- Refactoring or modernising the Linux logic itself (this PR moves it but doesn't change it)
- Updating dependencies — no new packages added; `psutil` was already present and is used by both Linux and macOS controllers
- Real e2e launch test (the scaffold is in place; wiring up a per-test `launch_app` monkeypatch is a follow-up)

author: ivgolovach
body:
## Summary
Passive and public mesh clients now only surface models that can actually accept HTTP inference requests. `/api/models`, `/v1/models`, and the console stay aligned when worker-only legacy peers or placeholder targets are present.

## Why
Passive clients could previously advertise models that were only present on worker-only peers or only resolved to `InferenceTarget::None`. That made the console look ready even though the next request could still fail with a `503`.

## What Changed
- treat only `Host` peers as HTTP-callable inference targets for user-facing availability
- compute warm status, node counts, active nodes, and mesh VRAM in `/api/models` from HTTP-callable routes only
- filter `/v1/models` and passive auto-routing candidates so models backed only by `InferenceTarget::None` are not advertised as available
- keep the chat composer disabled until `/api/models` reports a warm model instead of falling back to `status.model_name`

## Example
```bash
mesh-llm --client --auto
curl -s http://localhost:9337/v1/models
curl -s http://localhost:3131/api/models
```

With this change, those surfaces only report models that a passive client can actually route to successfully.

## Architecture
The mesh catalog remains broader than immediate routability: cold catalog entries still appear in `/api/models`, but only HTTP-callable hosts contribute warm state and route statistics. This keeps discovery intact while making client readiness and model availability honest.

## Validation
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `CARGO_HOME=/tmp/mesh-llm-cargo-home CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/mesh-llm-passive-visible cargo test -p mesh-llm test_http_route_stats_only_count_http_callable_legacy_hosts`
- `CARGO_HOME=/tmp/mesh-llm-cargo-home CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/mesh-llm-passive-visible cargo test -p mesh-llm worker_only_legacy_models_are_excluded_from_http_routes`
- `CARGO_HOME=/tmp/mesh-llm-cargo-home CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/mesh-llm-passive-visible cargo test -p mesh-llm test_callable_models_excludes_none_only_targets`
- `npm test -- App.test.tsx`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run build`
- `git diff --check`

## UI
The console now waits for a warm model from `/api/models` before enabling chat on passive clients.

The inbound matching gate in getPurchaseOrderData() used isInventoryPO_() which requires gl_project_name to contain "inventory". Since gl_project_name is only 73% populated and is a project name (not an inventory indicator), POs with real inventory items (e.g. ALS-GCPI-TTS-JKT-260303 with asset account 11-5010-001 Inventory) were misclassified as non-inventory and skipped entirely from inbound matching.

Changed the gate to use INVENTORY_SUBSIDIARIES_ instead, so all POs from inventory subsidiaries get matched to WMS inbound records regardless of gl_project_name value.

This pull request updates the AI Influencer automation pipeline, focusing on improved TTS (Text-to-Speech) workflow flexibility, enhanced documentation for TTS seed evaluation, workflow scheduling, environment variable configuration, and Discord bot command enhancements. The changes aim to make TTS generation more robust and user-friendly, support advanced seed evaluation workflows, and clarify operational procedures and troubleshooting.

**Key changes include:**

### TTS Workflow Improvements and Documentation
- Introduced a comprehensive "TTS Seed Lab" section in `README.md`, detailing tools and workflows for large-scale TTS seed evaluation, including quickstart scripts, auto-evaluation, reporting, and integration with RunPod serverless TTS. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efR1021-R1135) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL1014-R1161)
- Added documentation for a staged, rollback-capable migration to TTS Router with RunPod serverless support, including new environment variables (`TTS_API_URL_INTERNAL`, `TTS_ROUTER_MODE`, etc.) and operational instructions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efR609-R628) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efR647-R651) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL1098-R1279)

### Workflow and Scheduling Updates
- Changed the daily notebook creation workflow (`WF-10`) schedule from midnight to 07:30 KST and updated all related documentation and workflow tables. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL424-R442) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL500-R516) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL691-R723)
- Enhanced the YouTube source collection workflow (`WF-09`) to check for existing sources in the active notebook before fetching new videos, and to select only the latest recent video per channel. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL397-R427) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL500-R516)

### Environment Variable and Troubleshooting Enhancements
- Added and documented new environment variables for auto-report attempt limits, job staleness, and n8n workflow webhook URLs, improving configuration flexibility and clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efR609-R628) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-51bc2fd0c78a0489ce5283c8364edce068ce9e427fcfbee7ab8c46e785bd08efL664-R695)
- Expanded troubleshooting guidance for TTS Seed Lab and n8n workflow integration, including credential mapping and webhook URL updates for compatibility with new n8n versions.

### Discord Bot Command Improvements
- Enhanced the `/tts` Discord command to allow users to generate TTS candidates by either specifying an existing `job_id` or providing a custom prompt for new job creation, with input validation to prevent simultaneous use. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d41340b7bb8f9723c9eb09c1daa7d693bb78a1137ba268fb72484039cba1bd5eL322-R348) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d41340b7bb8f9723c9eb09c1daa7d693bb78a1137ba268fb72484039cba1bd5eR359-R401)

## Summary

  - added a new /wiki command to OpenClaude
  - implemented the first wiki MVP under .openclaude/wiki
  - added three initial wiki flows:
      - /wiki init
      - /wiki status
      - /wiki ingest <local-file-path>
  - introduced a small wiki service layer for:
      - path resolution
      - initialization
      - status reporting
      - deterministic local source ingestion
      - index rebuilding
  - this changed because OpenClaude needs a durable, repo-native knowledge layer instead of relying only on transient chat/session context
  - this MVP establishes the filesystem shape and command surface for a future “living wiki” workflow, while keeping the first version deterministic and easy to reason about

  ## Impact

  - user-facing impact:
      - users can now initialize a project wiki in .openclaude/wiki
      - users can inspect wiki status and ingest local files into source notes
      - OpenClaude starts gaining persistent, human-readable project knowledge artifacts
  - developer/maintainer impact:
      - creates a clear foundation for future wiki features like /wiki query and /wiki lint
      - introduces a modular wiki service layer that can be extended without rewriting command plumbing
      - adds focused tests around wiki initialization, status, and local ingest behavior

  ## Testing

  - [x] bun run build
  - [ ] bun run smoke
  - [x] focused tests:
      - bun test ./src/services/wiki/init.test.ts ./src/services/wiki/status.test.ts ./src/services/wiki/ingest.test.ts

  ## Notes

  - provider/model path tested:
      - not provider-specific
      - this is local filesystem and command-flow functionality only
  - screenshots attached (if UI changed):
      - no

      - /wiki query and /wiki lint are the next logical features on top of this MVP

author: nikorsanchez
body:
## Description:

Added reward system to quest completion, for now if inventory is full, reward is discarded. this need to be improved later.

## How to test:

As said in editor branch related with this issue, first create world like: 
```create a new world, create items if you want to reward items, create lootTable if needed too, then create a quest, then go by the button that set rewards, set the reward you want, navigate back its saved automatically, then you can add the quest if an npc is created with its dialog and set de quest on a message from its dialog. now if you try it in game client it should be added to the current registries and should be acquired by completing the quest.```

In game just simply complete a quest and check on inventory and hud if gold or item was acquired.

## Summary

This pull request adds new event channels for quest reward gold and items, and integrates them into the server-side character systems. The changes enable the `GoldSystem` and `InventorySystem` to listen for quest reward events and update player state accordingly. Additionally, the codebase is refactored for improved clarity and logging consistency.

**Quest Reward Event Integration:**

* Added `QuestRewardGoldEvent` and `QuestRewardItemEvent` event channels, including their asset and meta files, to handle quest reward notifications for gold and items. 
* Registered the new quest reward event channels in the `ServerEventRegistry` and updated the registry asset to include references to these events.

**GoldSystem Enhancements:**

* Injected and subscribed to `QuestRewardGoldEvent` in `GoldSystem`, handling quest gold rewards by updating player gold state when the event is raised. 
* Improved logging messages for clarity and consistency, especially in gold-related operations.

**InventorySystem Enhancements:**

* Injected and subscribed to `QuestRewardItemEvent` in `InventorySystem`, handling quest item rewards by adding items to player inventory when the event is raised. 
* Refactored inventory item pickup and purchase logic for better clarity, error handling, and logging.

author: michaelwest22
body:
## Description
when parsing trigger specs that have event filters with commas it currently splits this off as a whole new trigger spec breaking it part way which breaks the trigger spec parsing. We need to not split on `,` inside `[]` to handle this.  Ideally a full tokenizer could  handle this to any depth of square brackets but this adds a lot of code.  So instead we can do a simpler solution to handle commas one layer deep inside [] easily.  note multiple depth [[]] is the only not handled well case and this was not handled before well even with no commas.

Corresponding issue:
#3735

Added test and performed manual testing of many trigger spec formats to verify

## Summary

Adds the **beta AI chatbot legal disclaimer** inside the Brand Concierge **chat panel** (narrow drawer and expanded view), with links to Adobe’s **Privacy Policy** and **Generative AI Terms**. Expands **where Brand Concierge loads** so it is available across Experience League except on **Support** and **Premium Learning** routes. ---

## What changed

### Brand Concierge disclaimer
- Renders a `#bc-panel-disclaimer` paragraph **below the chat input** inside `.input-section` (not under the floating “Ask a question” pill on the page).
- Copy includes links to:

- **CSS:** centered small-body text; link styles reset so anchors match disclaimer size (global `a` rules no longer blow up link font); half-line spacing under the disclaimer; input overlay height adjusted for input + disclaimer; flex column on `.input-section`; bottom padding tuned so the disclaimer sits correctly in drawer and expanded modes.
- Floating trigger **z-index** raised so it stays above typical page widgets; trigger re-appended to end of `body` after init to improve stacking order.

### Eligibility (`delayed.js`)
- **Before:** Brand Concierge only on doc-themed or home pages.

- Existing **`bcAuthRequired`** behavior unchanged (e.g. Adobe employee check when enabled in config).

### Assets
- **`icons/bc-ask-sparkles.svg`** — updated gradient / artwork for the Ask affordance.

---

## How to test

1. Open a non–Support / non–Premium page where Brand Concierge is enabled; confirm the floating **Ask** control and that **no** disclaimer appears under the pill on the main page.
2. Open the chat **drawer**: disclaimer appears **under the input**, links open in a new tab, typography is consistent.
3. **Expand** the chat: same disclaimer and spacing.
4. Visit **`/{lang}/support`** and **`/{lang}/premium`**: Brand Concierge should **not** load (no pill / no panel).
5. (If `bcAuthRequired` is on in your env) confirm employee-only behavior still applies.

author: olimcfly
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete SEO content silo targeting first-time homebuyers (primo-accédants) in Aix-en-Provence for 2026. It includes a database seeder that populates 10 interconnected blog articles (1 pilier + 9 satellites), a comprehensive SEO strategy document, and the required database schema migrations.

## Key Changes

### Database Schema (`database/migrations/009_blog_schema.sql`)
- Created `blog_silos` table to organize content into thematic clusters
- Created `blog_articles` table with SEO metadata (title, meta description, H1, content, publication status)
- Created `blog_keywords` table to track keyword performance and Golden Ratio metrics
- Includes fields for content consciousness levels and article type classification (pilier/satellite)

### Content Seeder (`database/seeds/primo_accedant_silo.php`)
- Automated seeder that creates a complete 10-article silo structure
- **Pilier article:** "Devenir propriétaire à Aix-en-Provence en 2026" — comprehensive guide covering 5 key steps
- **Satellite articles:**
  - Buying without down payment (sans apport)
  - Budget calculation and simulation
  - Borrowing capacity with €3,000/month salary
  - Neighborhood guides (Jas de Bouffan, Encagnane, Luynes)
  - Rapid purchase strategies
  - Common mistakes for first-time buyers
  - Overcoming purchase barriers

- Each article includes:
  - SEO-optimized titles, meta descriptions, and H1 tags
  - Rich HTML content with internal linking strategy
  - FAQ sections and related article recommendations
  - CTAs directing to `/estimation-gratuite` conversion funnel
  - Word count tracking for content analysis

### SEO Strategy Document (`docs/strategie-seo-primo-accedant-aix-2026.md`)
- Detailed buyer persona (Julien/Marie, 28–38 years old, €2,500–€4,500/month income)
- Eugene Schwartz consciousness level mapping (5 levels from unaware to highly aware)
- Complete silo structure with keyword targeting and Golden Ratio scoring
- Internal linking strategy with visual maillage diagram
- Email nurture sequence (3-email funnel for lead conversion)
- Google Ads campaign structure (3 campaigns: high intent, long-tail, remarketing)
- Publication calendar and KPI tracking framework

## Implementation Details

- **M.E.R.E Framework:** Content organized by buyer consciousness level to guide prospects through awareness → consideration → decision journey
- **Interconnected Content:** Each article links to the pilier and 2 complementary satellites, creating a cohesive content cluster
- **Local Relevance:** All content tailored to Aix-en-Provence market with specific neighborhoods, price points, and local programs (PTZ, Action Logement)
- **Conversion Optimization:** Every article includes 2–3 CTAs funneling to lead capture form
- **Scalable Structure:** Seeder uses prepared statements and error handling for safe database operations

## Business Context
This silo targets a high-intent audience (first-time homebuyers in a competitive market) with educational content that builds trust while capturing leads for the sales funnel. The strategy balances organic SEO growth with paid acquisition (Google Ads) and email nurturing.

## Obiettivo

Aggiornare `mosaic/mosaic.sh` per fare in modo che tutti gli stream vengano mostrati in formato 16:9 senza deformazioni, usando `scale` con `force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease` e `pad` per aggiungere bande nere dove necessario (letterbox/pillarbox).

In **tutti i layout** (1, 2, 3, 4 stream) sostituire ogni occorrenza del filtro `scale` con la versione che mantiene il 16:9:

### Prima (attuale):
```
scale=${TILE_W}:${TILE_H},fps=${OUTPUT_FPS}
scale=${OUTPUT_WIDTH}:${OUTPUT_HEIGHT},fps=${OUTPUT_FPS}

```

scale=${OUTPUT_WIDTH}:${OUTPUT_HEIGHT}:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=${OUTPUT_WIDTH}:${OUTPUT_HEIGHT}:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:black,fps=${OUTPUT_FPS}

body:
Closes #2957

Partially addresses #2938

## Summary

- Add original-sound handling in the sound metadata flow for videos without a shared Kind 1063 audio event
- Enable audio extraction and publishing by default for all new videos (`allowAudioReuse` now defaults to `true`)
- Add `OriginalSoundDetailScreen` and synthetic original-sound support in sound detail routing

## Changes

**Metadata / sound detail flow:**
- `MetadataSoundsSection` now shows a `Sounds` section for videos without shared audio
- Original-sound taps create a synthetic `AudioEvent` from the source video and route into sound detail with source video context
- `SoundDetailScreen` can now render original-sound context and show the source video
- `OriginalSoundDetailScreen` and route helpers were added for view-only original-sound presentation

**Audio reuse enabled by default:**
- `allowAudioReuse` defaults to `true` in `VideoEditorProviderState`, `VideoEditorMeta`, and `DivineVideoDraft`
- New videos will extract audio, upload to Blossom, and publish Kind 1063 events unless the creator opts out

## Out of Scope / Follow-up

- The main feed overlay still only shows audio attribution for videos with shared audio
- Showing `♪ Original sound - @creator` directly in the feed on videos without shared audio is tracked as follow-up work

## Test plan

body:
## What

Adds a local image cache layer so card images are fetched from NRDB once and served from disk on subsequent displays.

## Design

- **`diskcache`** for TTL tracking and LRU eviction metadata (SQLite-backed, thread-safe)
- Plain `{code}.jpg` files in `data/card_images/` for direct Gradio serving
- No duplicate storage — diskcache manages metadata only, images are the `.jpg` files
- Graceful fallback to remote NRDB URL on cache miss or fetch failure

## Defaults

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| TTL | 30 days |
| Size limit | 500 MB |
| Eviction | LRU |
| Fetch | Lazy (on first display) |

## Files changed

- `src/image_cache.py` — `ImageCache` class + singleton accessor
- `src/web_ui.py` — swapped `NRDB_CARD_IMG` URLs for `image_cache.get_url()`, added `allowed_paths` to Gradio
- `tests/test_image_cache.py` — 16 tests (hit/miss, TTL, stale refresh, errors, warm, stats)
- `tests/test_web_ui.py` — stub cache injected for existing tests

## Code review findings addressed

- Fixed `cache_dir` variable scope bug (would crash `main()`)
- Eliminated sidecar pattern that caused stale files after TTL expiry
- Added test for stale file replacement on TTL expiry

## Scaling path

Swap `diskcache.Cache` → `FanoutCache` (sharded) or Redis/S3 for the storage backend.

author: sayinel
body:
## Summary

Complete implementation of the Vault System (§80-§90) from `docs/design/part12-vault-system.md`. This adds multi-vault context management, cross-vault wikilinks, standalone file editing, and comprehensive settings resolution.

## Motivation

Baram previously operated in single-vault mode. Users need to work with multiple knowledge bases simultaneously (e.g., a work vault + a journal vault), link documents across vaults, and quickly preview external files without adding them to a vault.

## Design Considerations

### Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Context Tab Bar                             │
│ [Work Vault] [Journal] [+]                  │
├─────────┬───────────────────────────────────┤
│FileTree │ Tab Bar                           │
│(active  │ doc.md │ note.md │ 📎 ext.md     │
│ vault)  ├───────────────────────────────────┤
│         │ Editor                            │
│         │                                   │
└─────────┴───────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **ContextManager (Rust)**: Per-vault path validation, alias registry, config loading
- **contextStore (Zustand)**: Multi-context state with persist, auto-alias generation
- **FileContext**: Invisible context for vault boundary check only; tabs are "global" across all vaults
- **File-mode window**: Separate WebviewWindow for tab tear-off with same Tiptap editor

### Key Decisions

- **Vault detection**: `.baram/config.json` vault section presence (not directory existence)
- **Cross-vault syntax**: `[[alias::target]]` with case-insensitive alias matching
- **External file tabs**: Global visibility across all contexts (no context switching needed)
- **Settings cascade**: Global → Vault (.baram/config.json) → Frontmatter (3-tier)
- **Graph All mode**: Fetch indices per-vault via explicit root_path, vault-colored nodes, dashed cross-vault edges

## Implementation

### §80-§81: Context Model & Workspace
- `ContextManager` Rust struct with add/remove/validate_path/resolve_alias
- `contextStore` Zustand store with persist, auto-alias, journal pinning
- 15 IPC commands registered in `ipc-registry.json`
- `import_file` IPC for external file drag-drop (destination-only vault check)

### §82: Context Tab Bar UI
- Full multi-context tab bar with drag-to-reorder
- Right-click context menu (rename, alias, color, close)
- FileContexts hidden from tab bar

### §83-§84: Editor Tabs & Search
- Context color dot on editor tabs, click to switch context
- External file tabs with ExternalLink icon, visible across all contexts
- Global search with 3 scopes: Current / Vaults / All

### §85: Journal System
- Journal context auto-creation with position pinning
- Work log utility per vault
- Guard against journal recreation after user closes all contexts

### §86: Settings Resolution (3-Tier)
- `resolve_settings` Rust IPC: global + vault config merge
- `resolveSettings()` TypeScript: global → vault → frontmatter
- Settings Vault tab: Initialize as Vault / Revert to Folder

### §87: Cross-vault Links
- `[[alias::target]]` parser in InputRule, SyntaxReveal expand/collapse, pipeline
- Cross-vault wikilink suggest with folder-grouped autocomplete (D-style UI)
- Cross-vault navigation with async IPC fallback for non-active vaults
- Graph View: `crossVault` flag on LinkEdge, dashed purple edges, vault-colored nodes
- Graph All mode: per-vault index fetch, scope filter includes all vault paths

### §88: ContextManager Backend
- Per-context LinkIndex/SearchIndex/FileWatcher (HashMap keyed by path)
- `validate_path_any()` for cross-context file access
- Symlink-safe `resolve_canonical()`

### §89: FileContext & Standalone Files
- `ensureFileContext` before `readFile` for vault check pass
- External files open as global tabs (no context switch)
- Tab tear-off to file-mode WebviewWindow
- File-mode editor: auto-save, theme, source mode (CodeMirror)
- Sidebar hidden when external tab active
- `tauriStorage` no-op in file-mode windows (prevents session overwrite)
- Virtual tab registration for image path resolution

### §90: App Startup & Migration
- `lastOpenedFolder` → VaultContext/FolderContext auto-migration
- Stale context cleanup on startup
- HomeScreen "New Vault" button
- Cold start file-mode redirect
- `processOpenedUrls` after vault restoration (race condition fix)

## Documentation
- User Guide: new "Vault & Context System" section
- FAQ: 6 vault-related Q&As
- Design docs: §80-§90 marked as implemented
- CLAUDE.md, roadmap, next-steps updated

## Test Results
- TypeScript: clean compilation
- Rust: 253 tests passed, 0 failed
- Vitest: wikilink tests 68/68 passed, settings-resolve 16/16 passed, context store 10/10 passed

## Checklist
- [x] §80 Context model (Vault/Folder/File types)
- [x] §81 App workspace persistence
- [x] §82 Context tab bar with drag reorder
- [x] §83 Editor tab context dots
- [x] §84 Search scope (Current/Vaults/All)
- [x] §85 Journal system redesign + Work Log
- [x] §86 3-tier settings resolution (Rust + TypeScript)
- [x] §87 Cross-vault wikilinks (parse/render/navigate/suggest/graph)
- [x] §88 ContextManager backend
- [x] §89 FileContext + standalone file mode
- [x] §90 App startup flow + migration
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] All tests passing

author: montal95
body:
## Summary

Three silent bugs in the Framer Motion animation system, discovered during
post-launch review. None were visible without inspecting network requests or
testing with prefers-reduced-motion enabled.

---

## Changes

### fix(hero): replace bare anchor with Next.js Link
`<a href="/work">` in `HeroContent.tsx` was triggering a full browser
navigation on click — bypassing the Next.js router entirely, tearing down
the React tree, and making every page transition impossible to reach from
the home page CTA.

`<a href={cvfile} download>` is intentionally unchanged — it targets a
static file, not a route.

### fix(transitions): add pathname key to AnimatePresence child
`TransitionProvider` now calls `usePathname()` and passes the current route
as a `key` via `React.cloneElement()` onto the direct child of
`AnimatePresence`. Without this, `AnimatePresence` had no signal that the
tree changed between navigations — exit animations never fired, and enter
animations ran without the departing page clearing first.

### fix(a11y): respect prefers-reduced-motion (WCAG 2.3.3)
`useReducedMotion()` from Framer Motion applied in two places:
- `app/template.tsx` — `y` offsets and `duration` zeroed when reduced
  motion is preferred; transitions become instant opacity fades
- `app/components/Nav.tsx` — mobile drawer `duration` zeroed; drawer
  opens/closes instantly instead of animating height

---

## Files changed
- `app/components/HeroContent.tsx` — `<Link>` import, `/work` CTA swapped
- `app/components/TransitionProvider.tsx` — `usePathname`, `cloneElement` with key
- `app/template.tsx` — `useReducedMotion`, conditional `y`/`duration`
- `app/components/Nav.tsx` — `useReducedMotion` import + drawer guard

## Test results
- `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0
- No unit test changes required (animation layer not covered by unit tests)

author: isdaniel
body:
Extract INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE coalescing into a shared coalescing module
  parameterized by QuoteStyle (Backtick, DoubleQuote, Bracket) so all three
  destinations benefit from reduced round-trips:

  - INSERTs → multi-value: INSERT INTO t VALUES (1), (2), (3)
  - UPDATEs → CASE-WHEN:   UPDATE t SET col = CASE WHEN ... END WHERE ... OR ...
  - DELETEs → OR-combined: DELETE FROM t WHERE (...) OR (...)

  MySQL respects max_allowed_packet (80% safety margin); SQLite and SQL Server
  use u64::MAX (no wire-protocol size limit).

When Secure Boot is enabled, shim automatically loads specific extra files from its directory: revocations_sbat.efi, revocations_sku.efi, and any EFI files with the shim_certificate prefix. body:
Expose all coordination Ra system parameters through new coordination.* configuration options, following the pattern established in PR #15962 for quorum queues.

This allows operators to fine-tune Raft log and WAL behavior specifically for the coordination system without affecting other Ra-based systems (quorum queues, Khepri).

New coordination.* configuration options:
- coordination.wal_compute_checksums (default: true)
- coordination.segment_compute_checksums (default: true)
- coordination.wal_max_size_bytes (default: 64 MB)
- coordination.wal_max_entries (default: from Ra's default_config)
- coordination.wal_max_batch_size (default: from Ra's default_config)
- coordination.segment_max_size_bytes (default: from Ra's default_config)
- coordination.segment_max_entries (default: from Ra's default_config)
- coordination.max_append_entries_rpc_batch_size (default: from Ra's default_config)
- coordination.compress_mem_tables (default: true)
- coordination.snapshot_chunk_size (default: from Ra's default_config)

Each coordination.* setting has a fallback to its default value, ensuring backward compatibility. The wal_max_size_bytes parameter maintains the existing hardcoded default of 64 MB.

Implementation details:
1. Added macros for coordination defaults in rabbit_ra_systems.erl
2. Refactored get_config(coordination) to read from application environment variables with sensible defaults, matching the quorum_queues pattern
3. Added Cuttlefish schema mappings for all new configuration options
4. Added comprehensive documentation in rabbitmq.conf.example
5. Added schema validation tests in rabbit.snippets
6. Added dedicated test suite (rabbit_ra_systems_SUITE) to validate defaults

All configuration is explicitly passed to the coordination Ra system during initialization, making the data flow transparent and maintainable.

Backward compatibility: Existing deployments continue to work unchanged, with coordination.wal_max_size_bytes defaulting to 64 MB.

author: tytaniumdev
body:
## Summary

- Bumps `memory` in `api/apphosting.yaml` from `512MiB` to `1GiB`
- Root cause of user-reported "Failed to fetch" on `/leaderboard`: the API container was being OOM-killed under normal load, causing Envoy to return `503 upstream connect error / connection termination`, which the browser surfaces as "Failed to fetch"

## Evidence

Cloud Run logs around the failure window showed dozens of:

```
Memory limit of 512 MiB exceeded with 533 MiB used. Consider increasing the memory limit
…
While handling this request, the container instance was found to be using too much memory and was terminated.
```

OOMs were not limited to `/api/leaderboard` — they hit `/api/jobs/:id`, `/api/workers/heartbeat`, `/api/coverage/next-job`, and the per-simulation PATCH routes too. The leaderboard is just the most visible because it's a page users navigate to directly, and the fetch fails outright rather than silently retrying.

Peak memory was ~533 MiB — only ~20 MiB over the 512 MiB limit — so this is a gradual-growth situation rather than a runaway leak. 1 GiB gives roughly 2× headroom.

## Why just bump memory (vs. optimize routes)

Several routes are hitting the limit, not a single pathological one. A targeted per-route optimization wouldn't stop the container from OOM-killing on the next pressure spike. Bumping memory fixes it for all routes in one change. We can still chase per-route memory optimizations later as a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI lint/build/test pass
- [ ] After deploy, hit `GET /api/leaderboard?minGames=5&limit=500` and confirm 2xx response
- [ ] Load https://magic-bracket-simulator.web.app/leaderboard in browser and confirm rankings render
- [ ] Check Cloud Run logs for `Memory limit … exceeded` — should be absent post-deploy
- [ ] Confirm no new alerts from the Sentry "Error Spike" rule

## Summary
- Fix custom rule groups including country groups as direct outbounds in Sing-Box, Clash, and Surge configs
- Custom rules now route through the selector hierarchy (Node Select -> Country Groups) instead of bypassing it
- Added regression tests to prevent this issue from recurring

## Root Cause
When `groupByCountry=true`, `buildSelectorMembers()` returns country groups as direct outbound options. Custom rules were using this function to build their outbound lists, which meant selecting a country group in a custom rule would route ALL matching traffic directly to that country's nodes, bypassing the main selector chain.

## Fix
Modified `addCustomRuleGroups()` in all three builders to manually construct the outbound list without country groups:
- Node Select (for routing through the main selector chain)
- Auto Select (optional)
- Manual Switch (if exists)
- DIRECT, REJECT

Country groups are still accessible through Node Select, maintaining the intended hierarchy.

author: naturalkei
body:
## Problem

When `release-please` creates a GitHub Release but `npm publish` fails, rerunning the workflow skips publish because `release_created` is `false`. There was no way to retry just the publish step.

## Fix

Add a `workflow_dispatch` trigger with a `tag` input and a separate `publish` job. This allows manually publishing any existing GitHub Release tag via OIDC (Trusted Publisher) from the Actions UI.

## Usage

Actions → Release → Run workflow → enter tag (e.g. `v1.0.1`) → Run

Closes #25

body:
## Summary

- MCP protocol version negotiation (2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25) instead of hardcoding
- Null `arguments` fix: treat explicit JSON `null` same as absent, preventing tool-call hang
- Input sanitisation on all 5 write tools (`sanitize_name` / `sanitize_content`): blocks path traversal, null bytes, oversized inputs

- Symlink skip in `walk_dir` and `walk_convos` (prevents following `/dev/urandom` etc.)
- 10 MB per-file guard in both miners (project and convo)
- 500 MB safety limit in `normalize` and `split` before reading into memory

author: dbwiddis
body:
Move non-native Linux drivers and path utility classes from `oshi-core` to `oshi-common`, enabling reuse by both `oshi-core` (JNA) and `oshi-core-java25` (FFM) without code duplication.

## Changes

### Moved to `oshi.util.linux` (from `oshi.util.platform.linux`)
- `ProcPath`, `DevPath`, `SysPath` (`/proc`, `/dev`, `/sys` filesystem path constants)

### Moved to `oshi.util.driver.linux` (from `oshi.driver.linux`)
- `Devicetree`, `Dmidecode`, `Lshal`, `Lshw`, `Sysfs` (pure Java Linux driver utilities)

### Moved to `oshi.util.driver.linux.proc` (from `oshi.driver.linux.proc`)
- `CpuInfo`, `CpuStat`, `DiskStats`, `ProcessStat`, `UpTime` (`/proc` filesystem drivers)

### Kept in oshi-core (JNA dependencies)
- `oshi.driver.linux.Who` — uses JNA `UtmpxType`
- `oshi.driver.linux.proc.Auxv` — uses `FileUtilJNA.readNativeLongFromBuffer`

### Module metadata
- **oshi-common** `module-info.java`: added exports for `oshi.util.linux`, `oshi.util.driver.linux`, `oshi.util.driver.linux.proc`
- **oshi-core-java11** `module-info.java`: removed stale `exports oshi.util.platform.linux`
- **oshi-core-java25** `module-info.java`: removed stale `exports oshi.util.platform.linux`

### Tests
- Migrated 10 test files to oshi-common with updated package names
- Rewrote `CpuStatTest` to use `Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors()` instead of `SystemInfo` (oshi-core only)
- Added `TestConstants.java` to oshi-common test tree

### Import updates
- \~30 files across oshi-core, oshi-core-java25, and oshi-core-java11 updated to use new package paths

## Notes
- Package rename from `oshi.util.platform.linux` → `oshi.util.linux` is required by JPMS (no split packages across modules)
- Driver rename from `oshi.driver.linux` → `oshi.util.driver.linux` follows the convention established in the prior PR for Unix drivers
- This is part of the bottom-up migration toward moving Linux HAL implementations to oshi-common

author: kweronsx
body:
This PR fixes a long-standing issue (https://github.com/intel/llvm/issues/9789) where UR_MEM_FLAG_USE_HOST_POINTER was silently ignored in the CUDA and HIP adapters, causing the host data to be copied to the device instead of being mapped.

What changed:

Removed the dead EnableUseHostPtr = false flag in both cuda/memory.cpp and hip/memory.cpp. This flag was hardcoded to false with a TODO comment, meaning the USE_HOST_PTR path was never actually taken — the buffer always fell back to copying.

Enabled the UseHostPtr allocation mode by properly entering that branch when UR_MEM_FLAG_USE_HOST_POINTER is set. The hipHostRegister / cuMemHostRegister call was moved from urMemBufferCreate into allocateMemObjOnDeviceIfNeeded (i.e. it is deferred to lazy device allocation), which is where it already lived.

Added HostPtrRegisteredByUR ownership flag to BufferMem in both headers. This boolean is set to true only when UR itself performed the registration. It ensures cuMemHostUnregister / hipHostUnregister is only called by the owner, preventing a double-unregister.

Handled already-registered pointers gracefully: CUDA_ERROR_HOST_MEMORY_ALREADY_REGISTERED / hipErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered is now tolerated in allocateMemObjOnDeviceIfNeeded. This covers cases where the same host pointer is registered across multiple lazy device allocations (e.g. multi-device contexts).

Explicit copy constructors were added to BufferMem in both adapters to deliberately not copy HostPtrRegisteredByUR, making ownership semantics clear — only the original object is responsible for unregistering.

Conformance test update: CUDA and HIP are removed from the UseHostPointer known-failure list in urMemBufferCreate.cpp, reflecting that the feature now works correctly on those backends.

author: kewe63
body:
## Summary

`NativeFiatTokenV2_2` was missing `notBlacklisted(from)` and `notBlacklisted(to)` modifiers on all four EIP-3009 authorization functions. This allowed blacklisted addresses to bypass compliance controls via authorized transfers.

## Problem

The parent contract `FiatTokenV2_2` correctly enforces blacklist checks on these functions. However, `NativeFiatTokenV2_2` dropped these modifiers when overriding, creating a security vulnerability.

**Affected functions:**
- `transferWithAuthorization(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32,bytes)`
- `transferWithAuthorization(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32,uint8,bytes32,bytes32)`
- `receiveWithAuthorization(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32,bytes)`
- `receiveWithAuthorization(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32,uint8,bytes32,bytes32)`

## Fix

Added `notBlacklisted(from)` and `notBlacklisted(to)` modifiers to all four functions, restoring parity with the parent contract `FiatTokenV2_2`.

## Impact

Without this fix, blacklisted accounts could transfer tokens through EIP-3009 authorized transfers, completely bypassing the AML/compliance blacklist mechanism.

author: peter-sixhoj
body:
## Summary

- Move `dna.md` and `principles.md` from `core/` to `thinking-core/` in both `.claude/rules/` and `.claude-static/rules/` — no content changes, restructure only
- Create `nxd-practices/` as a sibling folder in both locations — empty placeholder, migration of NXD-specific content is a subsequent CR
- Update `rules/README.md` to reflect the new folder structure and remove the two moved file entries from `core/`
- Add decision record at `.claude-decision-records/rules/thinking-core-separation.md` covering the three warranted decisions

## Rationale

**Two-layer separation (D1):** `core/` held two distinct classes of content — universal thinking principles and NXD-specific practices — without structural distinction. No placement gate existed. Two sibling folders make the distinction structural and enforceable.

**Universality gate for `thinking-core/` (D4):** A file belongs in `thinking-core/` only when all three invariants hold simultaneously: Universal (no NXD/software/AI dependency), Timeless (survives context change), No domain dependency (no named tools, platforms, or org terms). All three must hold.

**Phase discipline — classification before reframing (D7):** A file is classified by its intent, not its current wording. If the intent is universal, the file moves now — imperfect wording is acceptable debt; incorrect placement is not. Reframing is a separate CR.

## Known debt (out of scope — reword CR to follow)

`dna.md` contains NXD branding and "We are..." phrasing. Five principles in `principles.md` contain NXD/software language. Both files travel as-is; a dedicated reword CR follows this PR.

## Blast radius

Changes to `.claude-static/` are distributed to all repos in the NXD-Solutions org. Impact: two files renamed/moved (`dna.md`, `principles.md`), two new directories added (`thinking-core/`, `nxd-practices/`). No rule content changes — path references in `README.md` updated only. Repos that reference these files by path will need to update; repos that load them via Claude Code system context are unaffected by the rename.

author: waqastakkar
body:
### Motivation
- The original classical featurization built a global `records` list and converted it to a single large `DataFrame`, causing OOM for large screening libraries and non-production memory characteristics.
- The goal is a production-ready, low-memory implementation that processes `screening_df` in deterministic chunks and writes features and failures incrementally to disk while preserving existing schema and semantics.

### Description
- Added a configurable `script_13b.chunk_size` (default `250000`) and wired it into `AppConfig` parsing as `chunk_size` so the pipeline can process windows of rows using `for start in range(0, len(screening_df), chunk_size):`.
- Replaced the in-memory global `records` approach with chunked helpers: `build_classical_feature_columns`, `build_classical_output_columns`, and `generate_classical_features_chunk`, and implemented `generate_classical_features` to process chunks, sort within each chunk by `screening_compound_id`, and write incrementally to `output_classical_feature_path` using `mode='w'` for the first chunk and `mode='a'` / `header=False` thereafter.
- Preserved training-schema compatibility by precomputing `expected_columns` before chunking and validating that training-required columns exist; failures produce rows with `NaN` for feature columns and an `rdkit_parse_success` sentinel column.
- Replaced deprecated Morgan fingerprint generation (`AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect`) with RDKit `MorganGenerator` via `rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator` while keeping identical bit semantics, and added chunk-level failure CSV append logic so `failed_classical_feature_rows.csv` is written and appended per chunk when enabled.
- Updated `main()` to call the chunked `generate_classical_features(...)`, remove/overwrite existing outputs cleanly before first write, read back only minimal columns for later applicability computations, and integrate returned metadata (rows/success/failure/feature counts and output path) into manifests and the JSON report.
- Added clear per-chunk progress logging messages such as `Processed X / N rows` and `Wrote chunk Y to disk` and kept deterministic ordering within chunks by `screening_compound_id` using `mergesort`.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall Kinase_Causal_QSAR/scripts/13b_map_screening_library_to_model_feature_space.py` which succeeded (byte-compile check passed).
- Attempted `python Kinase_Causal_QSAR/scripts/13b_map_screening_library_to_model_feature_space.py --help` but execution failed in this environment due to missing runtime dependency `numpy` (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'`), so runtime invocation tests were not executed here.

author: bpforbes
body:
- kernel/core/vfs/disk.c: Replace fixed-size 256-byte stack buffer +
  strcat(tmp, zeros) with a dynamically-sized heap allocation in
  update_cluster_line; stack buffer overflowed whenever g_cluster_size > 126.
  Also add NULL guard on malloc failure inside the fill loop.

- userland/shell/util.c (load_history): Use a temporary pointer for
  realloc so the original hist is not lost on allocation failure; return
  partial results rather than crashing with a NULL deref.

- userland/shell/interpreter.c (interactive_shell):
  * Guard realloc for g_interactive_history with a temp pointer; skip
    the history-push rather than NULL-deref on OOM.
  * Replace strcpy with strncpy+explicit NUL for history-navigation
    (up/down arrow) so a long history entry cannot overflow line[1024].
  * Add bounds check before line[len++] in raw-mode character input;
    without this a user typing >1023 chars silently overflowed the buffer.

- userland/shell/sh.c (main batch loop): Change totalLen from int to
  size_t to prevent integer overflow on large argument lists; add NULL
  check after malloc so a failed allocation skips the command rather
  than dereferencing NULL.

body:
### Motivation
- The retention policy was driven by a single shared constant which prevented applying separate hard-delete windows to public and private chat/audio. 
- The goal is to keep the existing automatic sweeper and purge flow while enforcing a 7-day public hard-delete and a 30-day private hard-delete. 
- Changes must be backend-only and limited to `chat.py` to avoid frontend or deployment-side effects.

### Description
- Introduced `PUBLIC_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60` and changed `PRIVATE_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60` in `chat.py`.
- Kept a backward-compatible alias `CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS = PUBLIC_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS` so legacy references won't break.
- Updated `_public_retention_cutoff_unix()` to use `PUBLIC_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS`, leaving `_private_retention_cutoff_unix()` using `PRIVATE_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS`.
- Preserved the existing scoped purge flow and sweeper cadence/locking; audio collection and public/private delete helpers continue to receive scope-specific cutoffs and are used in `_purge_expired_chat_data`.

### Testing
- Ran `python3 -m py_compile chat.py` to check syntax and it succeeded.
- Attempted `python -m py_compile chat.py` but it failed due to the local pyenv selection (`3.12.7`) not being installed in the environment; this is an environment issue and not a code error.
- Verified presence of new constants and helper functions via `rg`/search for the markers (found `PUBLIC_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS`, `PRIVATE_CHAT_RETENTION_SECONDS`, `_public_retention_cutoff_unix`, `_private_retention_cutoff_unix`, `_collect_expired_chat_audio_rows`, `_delete_expired_public_messages`, `_delete_expired_private_messages`, `CHAT_RETENTION_SWEEP_SECONDS`).

author: magicgg91
body:
### Motivation

- Reduce the number of Grype findings pragmatically by consuming fixes available in Alpine stable and by shrinking the runtime attack surface.  
- Keep the image on a stable Alpine branch (no `edge`) and avoid blind or unstable upgrades while improving reproducibility.  
- Make vulnerability tracking repeatable by adding an optional CI job to build and scan the image with Grype and publish reports.

### Description

- Pin the base image to `nginx:alpine3.22` and run `apk upgrade --no-cache` then install a minimal runtime set (`python3`, `dcron`, `gettext-envsubst`, `tzdata`) in `conf/Dockerfile`.  
- Replace the heavier `gettext` package with `gettext-envsubst` (only `envsubst` is required by the entrypoint) to reduce surface area.  
- Add a non-blocking GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/security-grype.yml` which builds the image, runs Grype (table + JSON) and uploads the reports as artifacts.  
- Document a reproducible local Grype command in `README.md` (`docker build -t mymedialibrary:local -f conf/Dockerfile .` then `grype mymedialibrary:local`) to allow local scanning before pushing.

### Testing

- Ran unit checks with `python -m pytest conf/tests/test_entrypoint_runtime_guards.py -q`, which passed (`2 passed`).  
- Attempted a local image build with `docker build -t mymedialibrary:test -f conf/Dockerfile .` but the environment lacked Docker (`docker: command not found`).  
- The added CI job is configured to run weekly and on manual trigger and will perform the Grype scan in GitHub Actions (workflow is non-blocking via `fail-build: false`).

## Summary

- Fix PC LUT blob heuristic: transformer models (exNorm ops present) need swapped pc2/pc3 assignment in the gap case vs CNN models
- Eliminates 20 PPU em=0x60 DMA-class diffs on SmolVLM l0_mlp (72 → 52 remaining)

## Context

The pc2/pc3 heuristic picks two 1024-byte type-6 blobs closest to the regcmd offset. For the "gap" case (closer blob doesn't touch rc_off), CNN models need closer=pc2 and transformer models need closer=pc3. Detection: check for exNorm ops in the op table.

This was tracked as a known follow-up in the source comments since PR #83.

## Remaining 52 diffs (not addressed here)

- 26 exNorm REFORMAT activation routing diffs (SRC/DST use wrong act tensor offsets)  
- 24 BS/BN blob diffs (template emits gamma/beta for exNorm REFORMATs, oracle has 0)
- 2 input/output BO routing diffs

These require activation memory plan analysis and are tracked on #80.

author: s1dd4rth
body:
## Summary

- PWA is now served over `http://localhost:8000` via `python3 -m http.server`, not `file://`. Service workers now register, caching works, "Add to Home Screen" produces a real installable PWA with offline support.
- Space Mono (regular + bold) and DM Sans variable are now self-hosted in `pwa/fonts/` (~70 KB total, OFL 1.1). Zero runtime network calls to `fonts.googleapis.com`.
- `install-ollama.sh` no longer writes a hardcoded `~/start-ollama.sh` stub that shadowed the real `scripts/start-ollama.sh`.

## What was broken

v0.1.0 claimed "private local PWA installable to home screen, offline support" but the install path silently broke all three claims:

1. `start-ollama.sh --chat` opened `file:///sdcard/ollama-pocket/pwa/chat.html`. Service workers don't register on `file://` origins, so SW caching never happened and "Add to Home Screen" produced a broken non-offline PWA.
2. `install-ollama.sh` never copied `pwa/` to `/sdcard/` in the first place. The README Quick Start told users to run `--chat` but the target file wasn't there.
3. `pwa/chat.html` loaded fonts from `fonts.googleapis.com`, and `sw.js` didn't cache them. Even if the SW path had worked, "offline" would still fail on the fonts.

Also latent: `ip` isn't in the default Termux package set, so v0.1.0's LAN IP detection was silently returning `"unknown"` on fresh installs. Fixed by adding `iproute2` to the installer.

## What this PR does

- **Self-host fonts** — `pwa/fonts/{space-mono-regular,space-mono-bold,dm-sans-variable}.woff2` with OFL license text and attribution. `pwa/chat.html` uses `@font-face` pointing at local files.
- **Serve the PWA over HTTP** — `scripts/start-ollama.sh --chat` now launches `python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind $BIND_ADDR --directory /sdcard/ollama-pocket/pwa` in the background, polls `curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8000/` until the port is listening (2s timeout, no `sleep` races), then launches Chrome at `http://localhost:8000/chat.html`. Background server is cleaned up via `trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM`.
- **Force Chrome specifically** — `am start -p com.android.chrome`. Samsung Internet and Firefox silently break the SW registration path; if Chrome is missing, the script prints the URL for manual copy instead of silently failing.
- **Symmetric bind** — `--wifi` exposes both Ollama (`:11434`) and the PWA server (`:8000`) on `0.0.0.0`. A laptop on the same LAN can hit `http://<phone-ip>:8000/chat.html`.
- **`install-ollama.sh` provisions the PWA** — new `copy_pwa_files` function copies `pwa/` to `/sdcard/ollama-pocket/pwa/` from the local repo checkout, with a GitHub tarball fallback for the curl-and-run path.
- **Install `python`, `iproute2`, `curl`** alongside `proot-distro`. Fixes the latent LAN-IP regression from v0.1.0.
- **Delete the `~/start-ollama.sh` stub** and fix the idempotency bug where `/root/.bashrc` was gaining a duplicate `PATH` line on every re-run.
- **Service worker `ollama-v3`** — cache bumped, old `ollama-v2` wiped on activate, asset list includes the three font files, fetch handler uses stale-while-revalidate for static assets.
- **README Quick Start rewritten** around a Termux-native flow (`git clone` + `bash scripts/install-ollama.sh`). ADB debloat path is an optional prerequisite. Three new troubleshooting rows.

## Design doc

Full tactical plan: `requirements/plans/B-pwa-install-path.md` (also added in this PR). Includes failure modes table, acceptance criteria, and manual test matrix.

Also added in this PR: `requirements/plans/scaffolding-system.md` (v1 plan for the upcoming app scaffolding system — this is the next track after B lands) and `requirements/REQUIREMENTS.md` (source requirements for the scaffolding system).

## Validation

- [x] `shellcheck --severity=error scripts/*.sh` passes.
- [x] `node --check pwa/sw.js` passes.
- [x] `pwa/chat.html` HTML-parses cleanly.
- [x] Sanity-tested `python3 -m http.server` locally against `pwa/` — all assets serve with correct byte counts, port-poll logic confirms readiness in ~200ms.
- [x] Grep confirms zero `googleapis.com` or `gstatic.com` references in `pwa/chat.html`.
- [x] Two independent reviews: internal plan review + outside-voice adversarial review (Claude subagent, since `codex` CLI was unavailable). Nine technical findings applied in-place. Summary of findings in the plan file's history.

## Test plan — needs a real device

The tests below need an actual Android phone with Termux. I can't automate these in the PR.

- [ ] Fresh Termux install → `git clone` → `bash scripts/install-ollama.sh` → install completes, `/sdcard/ollama-pocket/pwa/chat.html` exists, `~/start-ollama.sh` does **not** exist.
- [ ] Re-run the installer — no duplicate `export PATH=...` lines in `/root/.bashrc`.
- [ ] `bash scripts/start-ollama.sh --wifi --chat` — console prints `PWA: http://<ip>:8000/chat.html`, Chrome opens, DevTools → Application → Service Workers shows `sw.js` activated.
- [ ] DevTools → Network — zero requests to `fonts.googleapis.com` or `fonts.gstatic.com`.
- [ ] DevTools → Application → Cache Storage → `ollama-v3` — contains chat.html, manifest.json, icon.svg, all three font files.
- [ ] Send a chat message. Ctrl+C the Termux session. `ps | grep http.server` shows no orphan Python process.
- [ ] Airplane mode → reopen `http://localhost:8000/chat.html` → page loads from cache, fonts render correctly.
- [ ] Chrome overflow menu → "Install app" → PWA installs to home screen. Launch from home screen in airplane mode → PWA opens standalone.
- [ ] From a laptop on the same WiFi → `http://<phone-ip>:8000/chat.html` → PWA loads on the laptop, chat works against the phone's Ollama.
- [ ] `bash scripts/start-ollama.sh` (no flags) — works as before, no PWA server started.

## Not in this PR

- Vendor-agnostic debloat (Plan A, closes #8) — separate PR.
- One-liner `curl | bash` install (Plan D) — separate PR.
- Benchmark harness (Plan E) — separate PR.
- Scaffolding system — separate PRs, after all four landing tracks above merge.
- Automated PWA tests (Plan F) — deferred until there's a second person editing `chat.html`.

### Contexto
chore: ajustes de configuracao e fluxo

Database configuration variable was renamed from POSTGRES_SERVER to POSTGRES_HOST, which can break startup if runtime configuration is not updated consistently.

### Plano 
## Approach
Complete the forward migration from POSTGRES_SERVER to POSTGRES_HOST by updating all configuration files, examples, and documentation that reference the old variable name. The rename in backend/app/core/config.py is already complete and correct, so we propagate it to all dependent configuration artifacts.

## Relevant Files
- .env.example
- docker-compose.yml
- README.md

## Steps
1. [modify] `.env.example`
   What: Rename the environment variable from POSTGRES_SERVER to POSTGRES_HOST
   Why: Ensures the example environment file matches the updated code configuration, preventing startup failures for new deployments or developers

2. [modify] `docker-compose.yml`
   What: Update all environment variable references from POSTGRES_SERVER to POSTGRES_HOST in service definitions that configure the database connection
   Why: Ensures Docker-based deployments pass the correct environment variable name to containers, preventing connection failures

3. [modify] `README.md`
   What: Replace all occurrences of POSTGRES_SERVER with POSTGRES_HOST in setup, configuration, and environment variable documentation sections
   Why: Prevents developer confusion and ensures documentation accurately reflects the current configuration schema

## Risk: medium
The configuration variable rename requires synchronized updates to runtime environment variables in all deployed environments (dev, staging, production). If existing deployments still use POSTGRES_SERVER in their actual environment configuration, the application will fail to start after deploying code with this change. Deployment coordination is required to update environment variables before or during the code deployment. The fix itself is straightforward with no code logic changes, but the operational synchronization requirement elevates risk to medium.

body: ## What this PR is trying to do Reduce benchmark workflow glue in memagent while keeping current behavior intact. ## Change 1: parse step simplification What we are trying to do: - stop hand-wiring separate parse/copy steps for every benchmark-action JSON file. What changed: - competitive + rate parse now run through one parse step using a file glob. Why: - fewer moving pieces, less workflow maintenance noise. ## Change 2: artifact collection simplification What we are trying to do: - remove custom shell copy logic for normalized OTLP outputs. What changed: - OTLP temp outputs are uploaded directly by pattern. Why: - reduces bespoke bash logic and output wiring. ## Change 3: dashboard fetch client simplification What we are trying to do: - rely on stock benchkit fetch behavior instead of local compatibility fallback code. What changed: - removed local try/catch fallback paths in `o11y-client.js`. Why: - one source of truth for fetch semantics. ## Important non-goal This PR does **not** try to redesign or hand off our `bench-data` branch/index strategy. That larger simplification is tracked separately so we can evaluate alternatives with o11ykit maintainers. ## Validation - workflow YAML parse check - `actionlint` on benchmark workflow - JS syntax check for dashboard client ## Related discussion Outcome-focused o11ykit issue with alternatives: - https://github.com/strawgate/o11ykit/issues/68 > [!NOTE] > ### Reduce benchmark workflow glue by uploading OTLP files directly from /tmp > - Removes the intermediate 'Collect normalized OTLP files' step that copied outputs into `benchkit-otlp/`; OTLP JSON files are now uploaded directly from `/tmp` using a glob pattern. > - Renames the throughput parsing step and its run-id suffix from `--competitive-otlp` to `--throughput-otlp` to align with stock o11ykit conventions. > - Removes local file fallbacks in [`o11y-client.js`](https://github.com/strawgate/memagent/pull/1835/files#diff-47bc58b3d1668a5904bf40c36f20f300e430b6d188f536b896f9d48d523ef019): `fetchBenchIndex` and `fetchBenchRun` now return `null` on failure instead of loading from `data/`. > - Behavioral Change: artifact upload now errors if no matching OTLP files are found (`if-no-files-found: error`). > > > > Macroscope summarized 4da204f. > >

author: bendavis78
body:
## GNOME 50 support

Adds GNOME 50 to the supported shell versions and fixes Super key detection, which silently broke in GNOME 50 due to a modifier mask change.

### esbuild bump to ^0.28.0

`esbuild-sass-plugin@3.7.0` requires `esbuild >= 0.27.3` as a peer dep. The previous `^0.25.10` pin caused `npm install` to fail with a dependency resolution error.

### Super key modifier detection

`global.get_pointer()` returns XKB-serialized modifiers where Super is reported as `MOD4_MASK` (bit 6), not `SUPER_MASK` (bit 26). `SUPER_MASK` is a virtual modifier absent from the XKB state returned by `xkb_state_serialize_mods()`, so any feature that checks for Super (e.g. Super+drag to tile) was a silent no-op on GNOME 50.

Alt was already handled correctly via `MOD1_MASK`; this brings Super in line with the same approach. Also consistent with Mutter commit c0fd2d9556 ("core: Let key presses of special modifiers through"), which changed overlay key handling to propagate the initial Super press rather than consume it.

Closes domferr/tilingshell#531

body:
## Summary
This change isolates localStorage data in preview builds by prefixing all storage keys with a unique identifier, preventing preview data from overwriting production data in the browser.

## Key Changes
- Added `VITE_STORAGE_PREFIX` environment variable support that gets prepended to all localStorage keys
- Updated all storage key definitions (`exercises`, `sessions`, `sessionSets`, `nextId`, `categories`) to use the dynamic prefix
- Added TypeScript type definitions for the `VITE_STORAGE_PREFIX` environment variable in `globals.d.ts`
- Modified the preview workflow to set `VITE_STORAGE_PREFIX` to `preview_pr{PR_NUMBER}_` during preview builds

## Implementation Details
- The prefix is read from `import.meta.env.VITE_STORAGE_PREFIX` at module load time, defaulting to an empty string for production builds
- This ensures preview builds (e.g., `preview_pr42_lt_exercises`) maintain completely separate storage from production builds (`lt_exercises`)
- The solution is transparent to the rest of the codebase—all storage operations continue to use the same key names, with prefixing handled automatically

author: berntpopp
body:
## Summary
- New `app/src/composables/useAuth.ts` — single owner of auth state (token, user, expiry, refresh, 401 coordination) with a module-level singleton so every `useAuth()` caller sees the same reactive state.
- New `app/src/composables/useAuth.spec.ts` — 25 tests covering the 5 required cases from plan §3 Phase E.E7: login stores token+user, logout clears both, expired tokens refresh (+ RFC 7519 boundary lock + malformed-body coverage), corrupt `localStorage.user` does not crash navigation, and 401-interceptor coordination.
- Migrates the 5 locked call sites off direct `localStorage.token` / `localStorage.user` reads:
  - `app/src/router/routes.ts` — replaces an 18x-duplicated `beforeEnter` body with a single `createAuthGuard(allowed_roles)` factory driven by `useAuth`.
  - `app/src/components/AppNavbar.vue` — `isUserLoggedIn`, `checkSigninWithJWT`, `setUserFromJWT`, `clearUserData` all read/write via `useAuth`.
  - `app/src/components/small/LogoutCountdownBadge.vue` — `doUserLogOut`, `refreshWithJWT`, `signinWithJWT`, `updateDiffs` use `useAuth`; the three stale "TODO: move to a mixin" comments are deleted.
  - `app/src/views/LoginView.vue` — two-step login flow now finalises through `auth.login(token, user)`.
  - `app/src/views/UserView.vue` — mount/refresh/profile/password flows all route through `useAuth`.
- Closes the P1 "Frontend auth/session state is duplicated" review finding (spec Appendix C) and Phase E.E7 exit criterion (`.plans/v11.0/phase-e.md` §3 Phase E.E7).

## Code-review fixes applied (post-opening)
- **I1**: removed dead SSR guards in `syncFromStorage` — SysNDD is a Vite SPA, not SSR'd. The `typeof localStorage !== 'undefined'` checks contradicted every other function (login/logout/refresh/handle401) that accesses localStorage unconditionally. Added a one-line comment at the top of the file documenting the SPA-only assumption. JSON parse-safety in `safeParseUser()` is unchanged.
- **I2**: validate `refresh()` response body before persisting. A 200 with a malformed body (`null`, `[null]`, non-coercible) would have passed `String()` coercion and persisted the literal string `"undefined"` or `"null"` as the new token, masquerading as a valid session until the next request fires a 401. *Superseded by Copilot Fix 3 below, which replaces the string-coercion sentinel check with a stricter type check.*
- **I3**: two new tests (16 → 18):
  - `isExpired` boundary lock: asserts `isExpired=true` when `nowSec === exp`. `useAuth.ts` uses `>=` (stricter than master's `>` by one second, intentional RFC 7519 hardening — "token is invalid at or after exp"). A future refactor that flips it back to `>` will turn this test red.
  - Malformed-body coverage for I2: MSW-overrides `/api/auth/refresh` to return `[null]`; confirms `refresh()` rejects AND does not mutate `tokenRef` / `localStorage` / the axios default `Authorization` header.

## Copilot review fixes (second round, post-I1–I3)
- **Copilot Fix 1** — `safeParseUser()` now rejects arrays and requires the minimal shape the SPA actually reads. Pre-fix, `localStorage.user = '[]'` would pass the `typeof === 'object'` check (arrays are objects), leaving `userRef` truthy with neither `.exp` nor `.user_role` — `isAuthenticated` would read `true` while every role/expiry calculation silently returned `undefined`. New validation: non-null, non-array object; `exp` is a non-empty `number[]`; `user_role` is a non-empty `string[]`. Tests: `[]`, missing `exp`, missing `user_role` (+3 tests).
- **Copilot Fix 2** — `syncFromStorage()` enforces a both-or-neither invariant. Pre-fix cleaned up a dangling token when the user was missing/corrupt but did nothing for a dangling user when the token was missing, which would trick components that only check `auth.user.value` (e.g. UserView.vue's mount hook) into firing unauthenticated API calls. Symmetric cleanup is now enforced. This also resolves Copilot's low-confidence **I4** concern (UserView hydrate path) because `auth.user.value` can no longer be non-null without a token. Tests: dangling user → user cleared, axios header cleared (+1 test).
- **Copilot Fix 3** — `refresh()` strict-types the raw response instead of the earlier `String(raw)` / `String(raw[0])` coercion. Pre-fix, a plain object body like `{}` would coerce to `"[object Object]"`, which passed the I2 sentinel check (not `"undefined"`/`"null"`/empty) and poisoned the session. Now accepts only `string` or `[string, ...]`; anything else throws `Refresh returned invalid token shape` before any state / localStorage / axios-header mutation. This supersedes the I2 sentinel guard. Tests: `[null]` (updated message), `{ foo: 'bar' }`, `[123]`, `[]` (+3 tests; I2 existing test updated).
- **Copilot Fix 4** — `LoginView.loadJWT()` validates the `/authenticate` response shape with the same contract as `refresh()`. Pre-fix, a malformed 200 body would hand `undefined` to `signinWithJWT()`, which would send "Bearer undefined" to `/signin` and then call `auth.login(undefined, ...)` after the inevitable confusing 401. Now toasts and early-returns on invalid shape / empty string. No new unit tests (the existing LoginView integration coverage is unchanged; this is a defensive guard matching the existing error-toast pattern).

## Tracked for follow-up (not in E7 locked scope)
- **M1–M7**: minor nits, deferred.

## Scope clarification
The plan's acceptance `grep -rn "localStorage\.token\|localStorage\.user" app/src/` would still return ~80 hits across ~15 other files (ApproveReview, ApproveStatus, ModifyEntity, Review, RegisterView, CreateEntity, ManageReReview, composables/useStatusForm, composables/useReviewForm, etc.) — **these are outside the locked E7 scope and deferred to v11.1**. Within the 5 locked files + the new `useAuth.ts`, the grep is clean (remaining matches are documentation comments only). The task directive explicitly relaxed the acceptance grep to this locked-file scope; flagging the interpretation here so the reviewer can confirm.

Also scoped up inside `router/routes.ts`: the plan listed 5 guards (lines 348/380/406/432/458) but the file actually had 18 copies of the identical `beforeEnter` body. All 18 were migrated to the new `createAuthGuard` factory because migrating only 5 and leaving 13 behind would have been inconsistent within a locked file. Behaviour is unchanged per guard.

## Verification
- `cd app && npm run type-check` — clean
- `cd app && npm run lint` — clean (0 issues)
- `cd app && npm run test:unit` — 475 passed (35 files, incl. 25 in useAuth.spec.ts), 6 todo, 0 failures
- Host `make ci-local` skipped per CLAUDE.md Conda-R workaround (frontend-only change).

## Atomic commits
- `useAuth.ts` + spec (6 cases, 16 tests)
- `router/routes.ts` guards → factory
- `AppNavbar.vue` → useAuth
- `LogoutCountdownBadge.vue` → useAuth (+ stale TODOs deleted)
- `LoginView.vue` → useAuth
- `UserView.vue` → useAuth
- Code-review fixes: I1 (SSR guards removed), I2 (refresh-body guard), I3 (boundary + malformed-body tests)
- Copilot fixes: Fix 1 (safeParseUser array + shape), Fix 2 (both-or-neither invariant), Fix 3 (refresh strict-type, supersedes I2), Fix 4 (LoginView token-shape guard)

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Login flow smoke test (login → see user/token populated; navbar shows role dropdowns)
- [ ] Logout flow smoke test (logout → state cleared; navbar reverts to Login link)
- [ ] Token refresh smoke test (wait for countdown warning → "refresh now" badge; /auth/refresh succeeds and the countdown resets)
- [ ] Corrupted-localStorage smoke test (manually set `localStorage.user = 'bad json'` in DevTools → navigate to /User; should redirect to /Login without throwing)
- [ ] Array-shaped-localStorage smoke test (manually set `localStorage.user = '[]'` in DevTools → `useAuth` should treat as logged-out, Copilot Fix 1)
- [ ] Dangling-user smoke test (manually set `localStorage.user = '{...}'` with NO `localStorage.token` → hard reload → user is cleared, axios header cleared, Copilot Fix 2)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Two changes to address the issue where slow post-update transitions cause users to double-click and launch duplicate instances: 1. **Reduced cosmetic sleep delays in `_do_update`** (`igo/app.py`): The three `time.sleep()` calls during the update progress animation were reduced from 2.5s + 2.5s + 1.5s = **6.5s** → 0.8s + 0.8s + 0.8s = **2.4s**. These sleeps are purely for displaying status text ("解凍中", "インストール中", "アップデート完了") and do not affect the actual update logic. 2. **Single-instance lock** (`igo_game.py`): Prevents duplicate app launches using a Windows named mutex (`CreateMutexW` with `"Global\\GokaGoSingleInstance"`). If a second instance detects the mutex already exists, it exits immediately via `sys.exit(0)`. Non-Windows fallback uses `fcntl.flock` for dev environments. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Test the update flow end-to-end on Windows**: Trigger an actual update and verify (a) the progress dialogs are still readable at 0.8s each, (b) the app restarts correctly after the batch script runs, (c) the new instance acquires the mutex without issues - [ ] **Test double-click prevention**: While the app is running (or during update), try launching a second instance — it should silently exit. Verify the first instance is unaffected - [ ] **Test update → restart mutex handoff**: During auto-update, the old process releases the mutex on exit, then the batch starts a new exe. Confirm the new instance can acquire the mutex and no race condition occurs if the user also clicks the icon during the batch copy phase - [ ] **Verify 0.8s display time is sufficient**: The "アップデート完了" message in particular should be visible long enough for users to understand the update succeeded before the window closes. Increase to 1.0–1.2s if too fast ### Notes - The second instance exits with `sys.exit(0)` silently — no error dialog or "already running" message is shown. This is intentional to avoid a confusing popup during the update restart cycle, but could be changed if users find it confusing in normal (non-update) double-click scenarios. - If `CreateMutexW` itself fails (returns NULL), the app proceeds without the lock rather than blocking startup. This is a safe fallback. - The `_lock` variable is held in `main()`'s local scope for the duration of `app.run()` (Tk mainloop), ensuring the mutex is not garbage-collected prematurely. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/ea994d0abbd5408fb47b6e405419bb3e Requested by: @CochanHachan ---
